The FAQ below is in German, as is our working day.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. title: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting
description:
Prevention Analyst - Pentesting

About this role


We are looking for a Prevention Analyst - Pentester, to join our Prevention track. An attacker does not look at one server in isolation. They look at everything a company exposes to the internet and work out where to start. You will do the same for our clients, taking the attacker’s view of their external attack surface, seeing what an attacker sees, and doing what an attacker would do next.

That means reading the story behind an attack surface. A forgotten subdomain, an old login portal, and a misconfigured mail server may each look minor on their own. Together they can show how an organisation has grown, where its blind spots are, and where someone could get in. When you find a potential weak point, you dig into it technically to find out how far an attacker could actually go.

This is not a classic penetration testing role. The deep dive draws on pentest methodology and expertise, but it is not a full pentest, and you will not spend your weeks writing long reports. We focus on finding the high impact vulnerabilities that need attention now and getting them to the client in a form they can act on.

This is for someone with hands on pentesting experience who wants to work across many customer environments, sharpen their attacker mindset, and grow into owning complex prevention engagements end to end.

What you will do

  • Assess clients’ external attack surface as a whole, from the attacker’s perspective.

  • Identify gaps and weaknesses across the surface, not just within a single asset, and work out how they connect.

  • Run technical deep dives into potential weak points to establish how far an attacker could get in practice.

  • Separate what needs fixing now from what does not, and focus on high and critical findings with immediate impact.

  • Turn technical findings into short, clear advice that clients can understand and act on.

  • Share what you learn with the team and actively pick up what others know. We work on problems together.

  • Contribute to improving our approach, sharing ideas that make assessments faster, clearer, and more useful for clients.

What you will need

  • Hands on penetration testing experience and a solid grasp of pentest methodology, particularly for external infrastructure and web applications.

  • The ability to think like an attacker, to look at a set of exposed assets and see where you would start and why.

  • Good judgement about real world impact, so you can tell an interesting finding from an urgent one.

  • The ability to explain technical findings to non technical readers, briefly and without losing accuracy.

  • A collaborative way of working and a genuine interest in learning and growing with colleagues, not working as a solo player.

  • Comfortable working across multiple client environments in parallel.

  • Fluent English.

Nice-to-have

  • Certifications such as OSCP, BSCP, or CPTS.

  • A proven bug bounty track record or other real world offensive security experience.

  • Experience working with SMEs or mid market customers on security topics.

What we offer

  • A meaningful mission, protecting organisations across Europe from real world cyber threats.

  • Work with top tier professionals from national CERTs, intelligence agencies, and leading tech backgrounds.

description:
Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. The Navigation Native team builds the high-performance C++ engine that serves as the "brain" of our Navigation SDKs. This library runs directly on end-user systems (on-board), powering everything from mobile apps to in-vehicle infotainment systems for partners like BMW, Porsche, and Zeekr.

We solve the fundamental challenges of movement: transforming noisy GPS/IMU data into precise map-matching, managing complex road-network graphs, supporting routes and alternatives, tracking progress along a route, and providing "Electronic Horizon" capabilities for ADAS. Our work happens at the edge, supporting location frequencies up to 10Hz and ensuring a seamless experience even in tunnels or dense urban canyons.

  • Build and maintain the unit, integration, and functional test architecture for a C++17 library, and the CMake and CI pipelines that run it.

  • Turn real-world location recordings into regression tests, and define the quality metrics for map-matching, routing, and route-following.

  • Experience diagnosing hard-to-reproduce failures: flakiness, platform-specific behavior, memory and threading bugs.

title: Senior Growth Product Manager
description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.

Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data.

About Us

Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing.

Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo.

The Role

You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work.

Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked.

We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging.

What You'll Do

  • Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them.
  • Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads.
  • Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first.
  • Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own.
  • Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them.
  • Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers.

Hiring Process

  1. Application: your CV, plus a short answer about one metric you moved (what it was, what you shipped, what happened, and what didn't work)
  2. 15-minute phone screen
  3. First interview (60 min): a deep dive into product growth work you've done. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo.
  4. Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem
  5. Culture fit (45 min)

We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.

Requirements

You Should Have

  • 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS: you were accountable for a metric for long enough to see whether your changes worked. In your application, tell us which metric it was, where it started and where it ended, what you shipped, and what didn't work.
  • Product craft and taste: you love software and have used a lot of it yourself, so you know what a good product feels like. You keep scope small, work in short cycles with engineers and designers, run your own customer calls, and have well-reasoned opinions about UX.
  • An AI-native way of working and building: you've shipped an AI-powered feature and measured whether people use it, you prototype with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), and you're happy to open a small PR yourself for something like a copy change.
  • You do your own analysis: you write SQL, build funnels yourself, and know when a sample is too small to conclude anything.
  • Experience with technical products: you've built for engineers or data teams and are comfortable talking about pipelines, warehouses, and APIs.
  • Clear writing and comfort working async: we're a distributed team across 12+ countries, and most decisions happen in writing, in English.

The five years don't all have to be in a PM role. If you were a product engineer or a founder and owned a growth metric, please apply.

Good to Have

  • Data quality, data observability, data governance, or data infrastructure experience.
  • Experience with product-led growth at a company that also sells to enterprises.
  • Experience with Shape Up or another fixed-time, variable-scope way of working.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Compensation €120,000–140,000/year + equity.
  • Outside Belgium, this is a contractor position.
  • Fully remote (EU-based), with a Belgian office available if you want one.
  • In-person kickoffs every two months in cool locations across Europe, three days with the whole product and engineering team.
  • All the tokens you need, across all frontier models.
  • Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement.
  • A senior team that ships, across 12+ countries.

Our Values

We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful product and roadmap decisions.

❤️ Why you will love to join Soda

  • You own the adoption metrics: you decide how we measure adoption and what we do to improve it.
  • Lots of room to improve: we already have enterprise customers and usage data, and we've done very little growth work so far.
  • Your own engineering team: you'll work with dedicated engineers who build agentically, so your ideas get shipped quickly.
  • Be part of a transformation: data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it.
  • Work on your own terms: fully remote, flexible hours, colleagues in 12+ countries.

😡 What you might not love

  • Rapidly changing priorities: our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done.
  • Small numbers: we have relatively few accounts and feedback is slow. If you're used to deciding from consumer-scale data, you may find that frustrating.
  • No playbook: this is the first dedicated growth PM role at Soda.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Le Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.

Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.

Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de cinq ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée. Les travaux de la chaire incluent plusieurs doctorats et post-doctorats visant à faire progresser la connaissance du phénomène de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les aciers faiblement alliés et de la fragilisation associée, ainsi qu’à développer de nouvelles méthodologies de mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire, ou à améliorer les méthodologies existantes.

Le post-doc proposé ici, financé par EDF, vise à déterminer l'effet de l'irradiation neutronique sur la ségrégation intergranulaire, pour les matériaux suivis dans le cadre du programme de surveillance des effets de l'irradiation sur les matériaux des cuves REP d'EDF. Il est en effet important de savoir si de la fragilisation intergranulaire peut intervenir à forte fluence pour prévoir correctement l'évolution des propriétés de rupture. C'est donc une caractérisation qui vient en appui de l'interprétation des fragilisations mesurées dans le cadre du programme de surveillance. Le travail consistera à mesurer les états de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les états non irradié et irradié en utilisant la microscopie électronique en transmission (STEM-EDX). Contrairement à la spectroscopie Auger, la microscopie électronique ne nécessite pas l'obtention d'une surface de rupture sous ultra-vide, ce qui constitue un avantage pour des matériaux dont la tendance à la rupture intergranulaire est faible. L'acier de cuve a une certaine hétérogénéité de composition chimique locale à cause de la présence de mésoségrégations enrichies en solutés majeurs et en impuretés fragilisantes comme le phosphore. Pour juger des seuls effets de l'irradiation, les zones d'analyse en microscopie électronique devront donc être équivalentes en termes d'intensité de mésoségrégation dans les états non irradié et irradié. Ceci nécessitera une caractérisation préalable des mésoségrégations et un prélèvement ciblé des lames minces en zone ségrégée ou en zone non ségrégée par faisceau d'ions focalisés (FIB). Les travaux de microscopie électronique seront réalisés à Saint-Etienne (microscope Jeol NeoARM) pour l’état non irradié, et au laboratoire d'analyse des matériaux irradiés d'EDF à Chinon (microscope FEI Osiris) pour l’état irradié. Une méthodologie d'analyse des ségrégations intergranulaires a été développée pour ce type de microscope au cours de la thèse de C.Y. Hsu (2023) et fait actuellement l’objet d’un développement dans le cadre d’un des post-docs de la chaire (mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire du carbone par STEM-EDX).

Le poste est basé sur le campus de Saint-Étienne, avec des déplacements réguliers au LIDEC d’EDF (CNPE de Chinon, 37420 Avoine).

title: Software Engineer, Knowledge Engine  – Data Infrastructure
description:
The Knowledge Platform team builds Exa's knowledge engine. We continuously synthesize information from across the web and beyond into one of the world's largest open-domain knowledge graphs, with hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims. The work has two halves: construction pipelines that decide what to trust, and retrieval engines that decide how best to search it. Our goal is to give agents answers to any factual question about the world with unprecedented precision and completeness.

In this role, you'll build the knowledge construction pipelines: turning everything from a 100k docs/s web crawl to vendor datasets into a graph of what is true about the world, and keeping it correct as data changes.

This is greenfield work with a massive scope. There is no off-the-shelf system for building a model of the world from the open web, so you'll make foundational decisions, from how claims are represented and resolved to how trust is assigned and how the graph evolves over time, that everything built on top of it depends on.

What you'll do

  • Continuously synthesize the live web crawl, vendor deliveries and APIs, and other off-the-web sources into one typed graph: extraction that turns pages and records into ontology-shaped claims, each carrying its provenance, timestamp and confidence.

  • Bring every new source in cleanly: versioned, append-only history with schema evolution, late-arriving and corrected records, and replayable cursors, so every claim traces back to the exact delivery that produced it.

  • Decide what to trust: entity resolution across billions of records (blocking, pairwise scoring, clustering) into canonical people, companies, places and publications, then truth discovery that weighs source reliability, recency and corroboration to reconcile conflicting claims.

  • Keep that picture current and convergent: streams arrive continuously, out of order and at very different rates, so the graph is eventually consistent by design. You'll build incremental computation over change data feeds, where each update is a diff of what changed and every job is idempotent and resumable, so the graph converges to the same state however runs interleave, fail or replay, and readers only ever see committed, consistent versions.

  • Measure precision and completeness: labeled evals for extraction and resolution, per-source coverage and correctness metrics, and lineage that pinpoints which source or stage broke and why.

What we're looking for

  • You've built and operated large-scale distributed data pipelines in production over petabytes of structured and unstructured data, with Spark over a lakehouse format (Delta Lake, Iceberg, Hudi).

  • You understand incremental processing deeply: change data capture, idempotent writes, backfills and reprocessing.

  • Strong in Python and at least one systems language; you can read and tune Spark query plans.

  • You obsess over correctness, reliability and data quality as much as scale.

Bonus

  • Entity resolution, record linkage, knowledge graphs or ontologies

  • Information extraction or truth discovery at scale

  • Lance or other columnar/vector-native formats

Example projects

  • Take a new billion-row dataset from first delivery to queryable entities in days, not months.

  • Keep a graph of hundreds of billions of claims current with incremental updates, so a fact that changes on the web reaches it in minutes.

  • Build a system that knows every company and person in the world, with one evidence-backed record each, resolved across the web and every source we ingest.

title: Head of Customer Success
description:

Rivia is a data engine for clinical trial intelligence. It provides data infrastructure and AI-driven workflows for clinical trial teams, enabling biotechs to run studies more efficiently and to demonstrate which patients derive the greatest benefit from new therapies. Biopharma companies are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is frequently slowed by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia delivers a real-time, integrated view across clinical trial data, improving both trial execution and the evaluation of new treatments.

 

Our goal is for Rivia to become the new standard infrastructure for modern drug development, bringing new therapies to market more successfully at a fraction of the cost.

 

We seek highly self-motivated, motivated and talented professionals to contribute to our growing startup.

Sales owns the commercial pipeline and execution of renewal and upsell transactions, including commercial negotiations and closing.   • Combining leadership with hands-on execution. You love developing high-performing teams but are equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves, solving difficult problems, and taking ownership of strategic accounts.

  • Driving measurable business impact. You're energized by improving customer retention, demonstrating value, and identifying opportunities to grow customer relationships in close partnership with Sales.

  • Thriving in a fast-paced environment. You enjoy autonomy, ambitious goals, and the opportunity to influence decisions directly, without waiting for someone else to tell you what to do.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and coach the Customer Engagement and Solutions Engineering teams, setting clear standards for performance, development, capacity planning, and hiring.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior scientific, technical, and business stakeholders at biotech and pharma customers.

  • Translate platform usage into measurable outcomes, including time saved, costs avoided, and operational improvements.

  • Introduce scalable account segmentation, coverage models, reporting, and operating rhythms without unnecessary bureaucracy.

What excites us:

  • A background in life sciences, biomedical engineering, biotechnology, pharmaceutical development, or a closely related scientific field.

  • Experience with biotech, pharma, clinical development, scientific software, or other complex life-sciences technology customers.

  • Evidence of driving customer retention, renewals, adoption, and account expansion through cross-functional collaboration.

  • Strong understanding of SaaS economics and customer success metrics, including GRR, NRR, customer health, and renewal rates.

  • Ability to navigate technical implementations, manage executive escalations, and influence senior stakeholders.

  • A structured, hands-on leadership style, commercial judgment, direct communication, and urgency in a fast-moving environment.

What Makes You Stand Out

  • Deep familiarity with clinical trials, clinical data, or pharmaceutical R&D workflows.

  • Experience supporting strategic expansion in enterprise biotech or pharmaceutical accounts.

  • A track record of measurable improvements in retention, adoption, and customer outcomes.

Our Values

At Rivia, we are committed to excellence, continuous learning, and the success of both our customers and our team.

description:

Piomic Medical AG is an award-winning Zürich medtech company on a mission to change how chronic and acute wounds are treated. Our lead indication is diabetic foot ulcers, a condition with one of the highest mortality rates in healthcare.   • Hands-on skills in CAD and prototyping, including 3D printing

  • An independent, structured way of working and careful documentation

  • English, German is a plus

Nice to have

  • Experience with plastics, silicone or injection-molded parts

  • Interest in regulated products such as medical devices

What we offer

  • ownership from day one: your designs become working prototypes that go into testing

  • Hands-on impact on a breakthrough therapy for one of the deadliest conditions in healthcare

  • First-hand experience of how medical devices are developed under European and US regulatory requirements

  • A paid position with competitive pay

  • Hybrid work and a modern open workspace directly at the Zurich HB

  • Flexible hours that fit around your lectures and exams

How to apply

title: Principal Design Engineer - Mechanical Equipment (80-100%)
description:
Lead technically by doing. 

Join our Design Engineering team as a highly experienced individual contributor. You will take on challenging mechanical design problems yourself, from concepts and CAD models to manufacturing drawings, prototypes and tested hardware, while helping the wider team make strong technical decisions. 

As a Principal Design Engineer, you are a hands-on member of our Design Engineering team, designing Climeworks’ CO2 collectors, the heart of our direct air capture plant. Improving how they perform, are manufactured and scale is central to the future success of DAC.

  • Mechanical concept & product design: You personally turn new concepts into robust physical products: developing mechanical concepts, creating CAD models, designing components and complete collector assemblies, producing manufacturing drawings, and supporting hardware through fabrication, assembly and testing.

  • Engineering problem-solving & risk reduction: Your experience helps you find the right solutions faster, anticipate problems early and reduce risk before issues reach manufacturing or testing.

  • CO2 collector design: You take mechanical systems from requirements and concepts through to detailed, manufacturable designs. You develop solutions, perform engineering calculations and make the decisions needed to create robust industrial hardware.

  • First-principles engineering: You use experience and first-principles reasoning to identify risks early, evaluate alternatives quickly and converge on simple, robust solutions. You apply calculations, tolerance analysis, design reviews and testing to reduce uncertainty.

  • Own design from concept to commercialisation: You work directly in SolidWorks to create and modify parts, assemblies and system layouts. You manage complex interfaces, packaging constraints and design changes so the complete system works together. You produce and maintain high-quality 2D manufacturing drawings, including appropriate GD&T, tolerances, materials, finishes and manufacturing requirements.

  • Prototype fabrication, assembly & testing: You stay closely involved after the CAD work is complete. You support prototype fabrication, assembly and testing, investigate issues and incorporate the learning back into the design.

  • Technical leadership & design reviews: You act as a senior technical reference for the team, supporting the Design Engineering line manager with design reviews, engineering standards and approval of critical designs. You support the extended team with technical judgement on complex mechanical design decisions, help maintain strong engineering practices and share your experience through everyday collaboration, mentoring and constructive challenge.

  • Cross-functional engineering collaboration: You work with manufacturing, testing, process engineering, procurement, suppliers and other engineering disciplines to ensure mechanical designs work as part of the complete product. You integrate external design resources where needed.


What makes you stand out 

Your experience makes your engineering more effective: you spot promising solutions early, expose weak points before they become expensive, and deliver designs that are clear, manufacturable and ready to perform in the real world.

  • Mechanical Design Experience: You bring 15+ years of hands-on mechanical design experience, ideally developing complex industrial equipment from concept through manufacture, assembly and testing.

  • Sheet Metal Design & Manufacturing: You have deep practical experience designing sheet-metal parts, structures and assemblies for manufacture at scale. You understand bending, welding and joining methods, forming, tolerances, material and thickness selection, and how design choices affect tooling, cost, assembly and quality.

  • CAD & Drawings: You are an expert SolidWorks user and remain hands-on with CAD. You personally create high-quality manufacturing drawings and are confident with GD&T and tolerance chains.

  • System Design & Engineering Judgement: You have experience designing from components and mechanisms through subsystems, interfaces and complex assemblies. You understand how decisions at one level affect the complete collector and can balance structures, airflow, movement, sealing, process interfaces, manufacturability, reliability and cost to arrive at robust solutions.

  • Manufacturing & DFMA: You have strong knowledge of machined parts, welded structures, materials and manufacturing processes, and apply DFMA to create robust, cost-effective designs.

  • Collaboration & Technical Leadership: You work effectively with engineers, technicians, manufacturers and suppliers. You share your experience, challenge constructively and help others make better technical decisions.

  • Education: You have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or similar.

    This job is not for you, if…

    • you mainly want to manage people or projects.

    • you mainly do simulation, concept work or system-level engineering without your own CAD work.

    • you have no experience with sheet metal, welded structures or manufacturing at scale.

Our promise: At Climeworks, you are accepted for who you are, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of background, identity, or experience. Studies show that women and individuals from minority backgrounds often only apply for jobs when they meet 100% of the listed criteria. If this sounds like you, don’t hold back. If you think you’d make a great fit for this role, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t check every single box. Let’s tackle one of humankind’s greatest challenges together.

What we offer:

  • Time Off: Enjoy 25 paid vacation days every year, plus public holidays.

  • Flexibility: Work how it suits you best. We offer a hybrid work setup and up to 4 weeks of remote work annually within any EU country.

  • Ownership: Fair base pay paired with an equity package – because your contributions matter.

  • Family Support: Inclusive parental leave.

  • Continuous Learning: Dedicated budget to invest in your professional growth.

  • Referral Rewards: Help us grow our team and earn bonuses for your successful referrals.

The short version

Plenty of companies are still running AI pilots. We moved past that a while ago: AI agents and human experts create, localise, check and refresh content for global B2B brands every day, across markets and languages. The next question is a harder one: not how to make content, but which content a client should make at all. That's where you come in.

As an AI Builder, you work on both sides of that. About half your time goes to bringing new clients live. The rest goes to building the intelligence that tells each client what to make next: where competitors outrank them, which pages are losing ground and need a refresh, which topics are an opening nobody has claimed yet, and whether they show up when people ask ChatGPT or Google instead of searching.

We've built our own CRM; our teams work with agents that do everything from setting up a tailor-made demo for a prospect to preparing sales calls and routing client feedback to the right person, and people across the company build their own tools. If you want to do serious work with AI, this is a good place for it. Everyone here is already building.

What Contentoo does

Most content tools make the client the editor. Most agencies make them the project manager. We'd rather make them the approver: they brief, review, and approve, and we run everything in between, inside their own workflow and tools. That makes us a product with a large service layer, sitting where SaaS, service and AI overlap.

None of that works without good foundations, so that's where we start. Before any agent runs, we capture what makes a client's content theirs: strategy, tone, terminology, compliance rules and hero pieces, per language and market, confirmed by the client. Every agent, expert and signal draws on that brand context. Skip it, and you get generic content, faster.

There's no shortage of software that tells a client what to write. The difference is that we get those foundations right first and then actually do the work. We've been doing that for ten years: 300+ brands, 300,000+ completed projects and 49 languages.

What you'll do

A suite of Workflows already runs in production, from localisation and creation to brand checks and content refresh. Each one combines AI agents with human experts and works from the client's brand context.

In practice, your week splits two ways. Half of it is implementation: getting new clients live, finding out where their situation is different from the last client's, and building the fix quickly, whether that's a new skill for their agent, a connection to their CMS, or a check only their market needs. Then you make that whole process faster and more automated on our side, so the next client goes live with less hand work.

The other half is the layer on top, which we're building right now: brand intelligence. Today most marketing teams guess what to write next. We want every client to know. Their own search data shows which pages are slipping, and a page that slips already gets a one-click refresh. Competitor rankings show where others win the topics the client should own. Strategy gets drafted from search data in each market and confirmed by the client, so every piece has a reason to exist. And every week we ask ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google's AI to answer the questions their buyers ask, to see whether the client is named or a competitor is. Every expert fix and every client comment flows back into the brand context, so the platform gets better with each piece.

What works for one client becomes a feature for all of them. And our own teams are clients too. Sales asks the CRM and the agents for a prospect's history before a call. Anyone in the company can ask Conny, our assistant on top of KIWI, our company knowledge base, how billing works or what a package includes. Product feedback from clients gets sorted and routed to the right owner by an agent. When one of those tools needs to get better, you build that too, with Claude Code, the Claude and GPT APIs, MCP servers and agent skills: whatever does the job.

The team

You join the Product team under Olivier (CPO) and report to Joost (AI Lead), in our growing AI team. You'll work closely with Jorge (Product Lead), Cesar (Tech Lead) and our development hub in Valencia.

Around you are the Connies: our people in Amsterdam and in our growing Valencia office. Once a month we stop for Success & Drinks, a company update with no slides and lots of energy, where anyone can take the floor to show what they've built. Wins get celebrated in #shoutout, from a sales call that nailed it to the talent team finding the right experts for a client's healthcare content. We play a padel tournament every year, run the city business run together (the ones who don't run come for the drinks afterwards), and take honest feedback seriously enough to train for it.

Who you are

You're a builder who gets energy from seeing a client actually use what you made. Three things come together in you:

Judgement. You quickly see what's really going on with a client, and you're as credible talking ROI with a CFO as architecture with an engineer.

You build. You prototype fast and ship, and you're at home with LLM APIs, agents, MCP, skills, and tools like Claude Code. You've built AI tools that real people use, and you can tell us what happened after launch.

Hands in the mud. You love being close to clients: fixing what gets in their way, building what solves their next problem, and owning what you ship. Under the hood, it has to work, stay up, and be safe. Your best hours go to the client.

You might come from strategy, product, solutions engineering, or technical implementation. Or you became the AI person at your last company and want a lot more of it.

Fluent English is a must; Dutch is a plus. We are looking for someone available 32-40h per week.

If seeing a client use something you built last week excites you more than perfecting the architecture behind it, you'll love it here. You'd be building on a business that's doing very well, with a large network of expert freelancers behind it: clients, data, and experts from day one, and an operation that keeps running while we scale. If you'd rather start from a blank page, a startup will suit you better. But if you want to make AI fly at scale, this is the place.

description:

  • realiseren van groei, kwaliteit en resultaat binnen jouw vestiging.

Lyceo heeft ruim 100 vestigingen en daarmee altijd een vestiging bij jou in de buurt. Wij zoeken vestigingsmanagers voor de regio’s: Bussum, Laren en Delft.

WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP


Details

Preferred starting date: ASAP

Weekly availability: full-time (5 days/week)

Period: 6 months

Location: Aerospace Innovation Hub, Delft, the Netherlands


About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced on-board UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers that are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members have a background in different fields such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub located on the TU Delft campus in the faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.


Your role

If you’ve ever spent a weekend building a drone, tuning a flight controller, soldering a power harness, or figuring out why your FPV setup won’t arm, this internship is literally designed for you.

We’re looking for a hands-on builder who loves working with real hardware:

  • wiring sensors

  • mounting compute boards

  • setting up flight controllers

  • testing drones outdoors

  • fixing whatever breaks and making it better

If phrases like ArduPilot, PX4, Jetson, ESCs, power distribution, 3D printing, or FPV gear make you smile, you’re the kind of person we want.

This is not a “sit behind a desk” internship. You will be on the drones. You will be in the field. You will fly.


What you’ll do

  • Build and integrate hardware onto real drone platforms used in active R&D.

  • Work hands-on with flight controllers (ArduPilot) and compute boards (Jetson, Orange Pi).

  • Deploy and debug embedded perception software.

  • Solder, assemble, and prototype wiring, adapters, mounts, and housings.

  • 3D-print parts and quickly turn ideas into working physical prototypes.

  • Support and participate in drone flight tests (you’ll fly regularly).

  • Troubleshoot issues, iterate fast, and improve our hardware setups.

You’ll see your work fly, literally!


Who you are

  • You’ve built or flown drones / RC systems (any level counts).

  • You tinker with electronics, FPV, embedded software, or robotics.

  • You enjoy making physical things work.

  • You like fast iteration and getting your hands dirty.

  • Linux doesn’t scare you.

  • You are independent, curious, and resourceful.

We don’t care about grades, we care about what you’ve made.

Please include photos/links of:

  • your drone builds

  • FPV rigs

  • electronics projects

  • CAD/3D-printed parts

  • GitHub repos

  • anything that shows you build things

If you’ve ever crashed something, fixed it, and sent it back into the sky — you’ll fit right in.


Requirements

  • Enrolled in a relevant study (Aerospace, Robotics, Electrical, Mechatronics, Engineering etc.).

  • Linux basics.

  • Interest in UAVs, robotics, embedded systems, or autonomy.

  • English proficiency.

  • Organized and proactive.

Bonus:

driver’s license, drone pilot license, CAD, 3D printing, soldering, or flight experience.

What we offer

  • 1000 euro monthly compensation.

  • 10 vacation days during internship period.

  • (Really) flexible working hours and option to work from home 2 days per week.

  • Have a direct and significant influence on highly innovative products.

  • The opportunity to iterate quickly with tight feedback loops, close to the product. We are innovating, learning is to be expected.

  • Responsibility over the things you implement, you are the expert on what you build.

  • If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself; this can be a resume, website or other source, as long as we get a clear impression of your background and skills.

  • If at this point we feel you are the person we are looking for, we’ll discuss the specifics (starting date and period).

ONE-Dyas is looking for a Production & ESG Data Engineer to ensure the accurate collection, administration and reporting of production, hydrocarbon and ESG data. You will turn complex data into reliable insights that support operational and business decisions.

What will you do?

·         Maintain and improve databases containing validated production and ESG data.

·         Collect and integrate data from production sources and operated and non-operated assets.

·         Prepare clear monthly, quarterly and annual reports and visualizations.

·         Support Production, Engineering, HSE and ESG teams with data supporting operational and business decisions.

·         Explore opportunities for automation, machine learning and AI to improve collection, administration and reporting.


·         A bachelor’s level in Engineering, Accounting, Computer Science, Environmental Sciences or a related field.

·         Experience in data engineering or ESG reporting, preferably within the energy or oil & gas industry.

·         Knowledge of database management, data visualization and data governance.

·         Preferably experience with Python, SQL or similar tools.

·         Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

·         A proactive, independent and team-oriented approach with an interest in sustainability.

Meet ONE-Dyas

ONE-Dyas B.V. is the largest privately owned exploration and production company in the Netherlands. As entrepreneurs in Dutch offshore gas and oil, the company aims to make a significant contribution to the energy transition, working at the forefront of sustainability and technological innovation. Extracting gas and oil close to home contributes to the national economy, security of supply, and climate goals by employing local services, products, and know-how, reducing the reliance on imported fuels, cutting emissions, and complying to the highest environmental standards in the industry.

With its roots dating back to 1893 in the mining industry, ONE-Dyas has a long history of successfully pioneering energy solutions. Today, its operations span the full lifecycle of offshore assets in the Netherlands, Germany and the UK, including the flagship N05-A development project in the Dutch and German part of the North Sea, set to be the first of its kind to integrate natural gas, wind power and green hydrogen. ONE-Dyas is also actively exploring carbon capture and storage, and green hydrogen opportunities as future energy solutions.

 

Headquartered on the Zuid-as in Amsterdam with around 150 employees, ONE-Dyas has a strong entrepreneurial culture, short lines across all disciplines and a strong relationship with its shareholders leading to a focused and effective work environment. ONE-Dyas has an excellent reputation in the Netherlands, the UK and Germany for its experience and skills across the entire oil & gas energy supply chain. ONE-Dyas is known for getting things done safe, reliably and efficiently.

  • AI in your daily work: you use AI tools every day in your security work

Nice-to-haves

Soft Skills

🧢 Goal-orientated, ownership and commitment

⚡️ Doer mindset - we are moving fast and we need people who can find the right balance between executing, planning and strategy

What We Offer

🏝️ Paid Time Off: 4 weeks (20 working days) of PTO per year to recharge and reset

title: Stage Bouw
description:
Hé stage topper! Kom jij, net als vele andere stagiaires, stagelopen bij Dura Vermeer Bouw en Vastgoed Hengelo? Bij ons krijg jij de kans om mee te denken, werken én ontwikkelen aan gave projecten binnen Noord, Midden en Oost-Nederland. Wij hebben weer volop stageplekken vanaf Februari 2027 op onze bouwen en op kantoor!

Dit wordt jouw stage

Als stagiair bij Dura Vermeer Bouw en Vastgoed Hengelo ga je aan de slag op ons kantoor of op één van onze projecten. We kijken in overeenstemming welke afdeling of welk project het beste bij jou en/of de opdracht past. Tijdens je stage word je goed begeleid door één van onze collega’s en krijg je de ruimte om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen! Jij staat aan het stuur van je eigen ontwikkeling tijdens je stageperiode: Hoe meer jij wil leren, hoe meer jij kan leren! Naast dat je zelfstandig aan een opdracht kan werken wordt je ook begeleidt door een senior collega die jou alle kneepjes van het vak gaat leren. We hebben door heel ons werkgebied verschillende bouwen waar we ruimte hebben voor een stagiaire, stuur ons vooral een berichtje zodat we samen kunnen kijken wat passend is!

Meer bij Dura Vermeer

Dura Vermeer is een familiebedrijf. Een onafhankelijke bouwonderneming actief in woningbouw, utiliteitsbouw, infrastructuur en techniek in Nederland. Al sinds 1855 vormen onze onafhankelijkheid en langjarige continuïteit de basis voor onze strategie. Met een omzet van circa € 1,8 miljard en ruim 3.000 medewerkers behoren we tot de top van de Nederlandse bouwsector. Samen realiseren we prachtige projecten. Iconische, en soms ook alledaagse projecten waarmee we nieuwe antwoorden bieden op maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Waarmee we de beste oplossingen voor morgen garanderen en het verschil maken voor Nederland, juist op de langere termijn. We hebben stevige ambities – en daarvoor geldt dat we die alleen kunnen waarmaken dankzij onze mensen. Als beste werkgever maken wij ons er daarom hard voor dat jij elke dag opnieuw kiest voor Dura Vermeer. Dat jij net zo trots bent op wat we maken als wij dat zijn. Dat iedereen die bij ons werkt gelukkig is. Dat je bij ons jezelf kunt zijn, je veilig voelt en je kunt uitspreken. En dat je tot je recht komt. En het beste uit jezelf kunt halen.

Hier zit je goed!

Wij zijn Dura Vermeer Bouw en Vastgoed Hengelo, een ontwikkelende bouwer in het werkgebied Noord-, Oost- en Midden-Nederland. Als onderdeel van de divisie Bouw & Vastgoed combineren we de kracht van een groot bedrijf, met de fijne sfeer en cultuur van een kleinere organisatie.

Bij ons vind je echte doeners en waarmakers. We ontwikkelen en bouwen, samen met onze klanten, partners en collega’s. Wat ons ons maakt? Gewoon dóen en gewóón doen. Dat zit er nou eenmaal in, en zie je terug in alles wat we doen.

Wil jij nou werken op een plek waar vakmanschap, samenwerking en heel veel plezier samenkomen? Mooi! Wij zoeken nieuwe collega’s binnen onze disciplines ontwikkeling, woningbouw, utiliteitsbouw, renovatie & transformatie en beheer & exploitatie.


Dit breng je mee

  • Je volgt een MBO, HBO of WO opleiding (pre: opleiding Bouwkunde);

  • Je bent proactief, nuchter en een harde werker, net als wij!

Dit bieden wij jou

  • Een stagevergoeding van €700 per maand op basis van 40 uren per week;

  • Je krijgt ruimte voor eigen initiatieven;

  • De beste collega’s om het vak van te leren en zij zorgen voor een ongekende goede werksfeer;

  • Een familiebedrijf waarin we voor elkaar klaarstaan!

Meer weten?

Wij beantwoorden je vragen graag of denken graag met je mee voor het invullen van je stagewens.

Schroom niet om contact op te nemen met Nikki Koehorst via 0628362285 of Hopelijk spreken we elkaar snel!

title: Agentic AI Senior Consultant
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Agentic AI Senior Consultant based in Netherlands.

In this role, you will act as a trusted technical advisor and hands-on engineering expert, helping enterprise customers design, implement, and scale advanced agentic AI solutions. You will lead the entire customer delivery lifecycle, from identifying high-value business opportunities and designing multi-agent architectures to deploying production-ready systems. Combining strong software engineering expertise, applied AI knowledge, and event-driven architecture experience, you will transform AI concepts into secure, scalable, and reliable enterprise applications. You will work closely with customer engineering teams, business stakeholders, and internal product specialists to accelerate the adoption of intelligent automation. Your responsibilities will also include establishing best practices for agent development, evaluation, monitoring, and governance while mentoring other technical professionals. This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of enterprise AI innovation within an international, customer-focused, and technically ambitious environment.


Accountabilities:
  • Own the technical success of enterprise customers' agentic AI initiatives, managing the complete delivery lifecycle from initial discovery and solution design through development, production deployment, ongoing operations, and advisory services.
  • Lead customer workshops to identify, assess, and prioritize high-value agentic AI use cases, translating business objectives into measurable and technically achievable workflows.
  • Design and implement sophisticated multi-agent architectures, including agent decomposition, orchestration, task delegation, tool integration, memory management, state handling, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Develop, review, and troubleshoot production-quality software using Go or Python, building agents, plugins, tools, and integrations that meet enterprise requirements.
  • Deploy and operate agentic AI applications using Docker, Kubernetes, and major cloud platforms, ensuring scalability, reliability, and maintainability.
  • Integrate AI agents with enterprise applications, data sources, and legacy systems through MCP servers, A2A protocols, REST APIs, and event-driven messaging architectures.
  • Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, knowledge bases, embeddings, and real-time event context strategies to improve agent accuracy and access to relevant information.
  • Apply the Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) throughout solution delivery, covering requirements gathering, architecture design, evaluation pipelines, testing, version control, release management, monitoring, and operational documentation.
  • Establish robust observability, security controls, governance frameworks, and responsible AI practices for agentic systems, including tracing, quality evaluation, cost and latency monitoring, access control, and auditability.
  • Advise customers on large language model selection and optimization across providers such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, AWS Bedrock, and Azure AI Foundry, considering prompt engineering, token consumption, costs, and model performance trade-offs.
  • Act as a long-term technical advisor, identifying opportunities for further AI adoption and helping customers progress from isolated pilots to enterprise-wide, event-driven AI implementations.
  • Conduct recurring technical reviews, solution health checks, and roadmap discussions aligned with customer priorities and annual planning cycles.
  • Enable customer engineering teams to independently operate, maintain, and extend implemented solutions through technical workshops, collaborative development sessions, and comprehensive documentation.
  • Develop reusable technical assets, including reference architectures, implementation patterns, accelerators, and best practices, to improve delivery efficiency and consistency across future engagements.
  • Represent customer needs and technical feedback to internal Product and Engineering teams, contributing insights that influence product development and roadmap priorities.
  • Collaborate closely with agentic AI platform engineering teams to resolve complex customer challenges, validate new capabilities, and contribute reusable agents, plugins, and accelerators.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to other professionals, helping strengthen agentic AI expertise and delivery capabilities across the Professional Services organization.
  • Communicate complex technical concepts, AI-related risks, and architectural trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Travel when required to support customer engagements, including occasional international travel.

    • Requirements:

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in professional services, technology consulting, systems integration, forward-deployed engineering, or enterprise application development.
  • Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience designing, developing, and deploying LLM-based applications and agentic AI solutions, including at least one solution successfully taken into production.
  • Strong understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, including version control, automated testing, CI/CD, and release management, with practical experience applying a structured Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC).
  • Strong programming proficiency in Go or Python, with Go considered a significant advantage.
  • Practical experience designing and implementing multi-agent systems, including task delegation, orchestration, coordination, and autonomous decision-making.
  • Familiarity with agent development frameworks such as Google ADK, LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI, or comparable technologies.

  • Solid understanding of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, vector databases, prompt engineering, and context management techniques.
  • Experience implementing evaluation frameworks, observability solutions, and security guardrails for enterprise LLM applications.
  • Strong knowledge of event-driven architectures, asynchronous messaging, distributed systems, and enterprise integration patterns.
  • Hands-on experience deploying distributed applications on cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform, using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Understanding of enterprise security and identity management practices relevant to AI systems, including OAuth 2.0, role-based access control (RBAC), secrets management, and data privacy.
  • Ability to independently lead customer engagements, make sound technical decisions, and manage complex projects with minimal supervision.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience facilitating technical workshops and presenting recommendations to senior stakeholders.
  • Professional fluency in English and either Spanish or Italian, both written and spoken.
  • Experience working with agentic AI platforms or enterprise messaging technologies is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with Solace Agent Mesh or similar agentic AI platforms is a plus.
  • Proficiency in both Go and Python is an additional advantage.
  • Experience with messaging technologies such as Solace, Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, IBM MQ, or TIBCO is beneficial.
  • Working knowledge of LLM platforms and services, including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini/Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, or Azure AI Foundry, is desirable.

title: Senior Scrum master
description:
Niet faciliteren om te faciliteren. Maar teams helpen slimmer samen te werken.

AI verandert de manier waarop we software ontwikkelen. Maar nieuwe technologie alleen maakt een team nog niet beter. Daarvoor heb je iemand nodig die mensen verbindt, samenwerking versterkt en verandering écht in beweging krijgt.

Bij adesso Nederland ontwikkelen we ons tot een AI First-organisatie. We bouwen aan moderne software, slimme dataplatformen en agentic oplossingen. Tegelijkertijd kijken we hoe AI onze eigen manier van werken verandert.

Daarom zoeken we een Scrum Master die verder kijkt dan Scrum events. Iemand die begrijpt dat Agile niet allen draait om ceremonies, maar ook om waarde toevoegen,  wendbaarheid, eigenaarschap en samenwerking.

Jouw rol

Als Scrum Master begeleid je multidisciplinaire teams die werken aan complexe softwareprojecten, data-oplossingen en AI-first applicaties.

Je helpt teams om beter samen te werken, obstakels weg te nemen en continu te verbeteren. Je bent een stevige gesprekspartner voor de organisatie, developers, product owners en stakeholders en weet wanneer je moet coachen, uitdagen of juist ruimte moet geven.

Maar je kijkt ook vooruit.

Wat betekent AI voor de manier waarop teams software ontwikkelen? Hoe kunnen AI-developmenttools en agentic workflows bijdragen aan kwaliteit, snelheid en samenwerking? En hoe zorg je dat teams nieuwe technologie omarmen zonder hun focus op mensen en resultaat te verliezen?

Je hoeft niet zelf te programmeren, maar je bent nieuwsgierig naar technologie en begrijpt hoe veranderingen in software engineering invloed en impact hebben op de organisatie, teams en processen. 

Wat ga je doen?

  • Coachen van Agile-teams op focus, samenwerking, communicatie en voorspelbaarheid

  • Faciliteren van Scrum-events die daadwerkelijk bijdragen aan verbetering

  • Signaleren en wegnemen van blokkades binnen teams en binnen de organisatie

  • Versterken van de samenwerking tussen developers, product owners, business en stakeholders.

  • Meedenken over de inzet van AI-tools om teamprocessen, kennisdeling, delivery en adoptie slimmer te organiseren.

  • Continu verbeteren van flow, kwaliteit en de manier waarop teams waarde leveren.

  • Bijdragen aan de verdere ontwikkeling van onze Agile-werkwijze binnen een AI First-organisatie.


  • Minimaal 7 jaar ervaring als Scrum Master binnen softwareontwikkeling.

  • Ervaring met multidisciplinaire teams in complexe IT-omgevingen.

  • Sterke kennis van Agile, Scrum en teamontwikkeling.

  • PSM I en II, CSM- of vergelijkbare certificering.

  • Interesse in AI, automatisering en de veranderende wereld van software engineering.

  • Het vermogen om teams, product owners te coachen, stakeholders uit te dagen en verandering te begeleiden.

  • Goede communicatieve vaardigheden in Nederlands en Engels.

  • Ervaring met SAFe, LeSS of andere scaling frameworks is een pré.

Je hoeft geen AI-expert te zijn. We zoeken vooral iemand die nieuwsgierig is naar de impact van AI op samenwerking en softwareontwikkeling en teams daarin kan meenemen.

Het team

Je komt terecht in een team van zo’n 25 gedreven medior en senior developers. We zijn groot genoeg om serieuze projecten neer te zetten en klein genoeg om elkaar te kennen. Iedereen heeft invloed en goede ideeën worden niet alleen gehoord, maar ook uitgeprobeerd.

We zetten onze development expertise in bij gerenommeerde bedrijven in Nederland. Daar bouwen we met Java en Kotlin aan oplossingen die ertoe doen, en we gebruiken AI om tot de best mogelijke resultaten te komen. We onderzoeken continu hoe AI ons werk en dat van onze klanten slimmer kan maken.

Ontwikkeling staat voorop. Tijdens onze kennisavonden delen we wat we leren en we bezoeken jaarlijks (inter)nationale conferenties om scherp te blijven. Daarnaast spreken we regelmatig af voor informele activiteiten, want goed samenwerken begint met elkaar écht kennen.

Waarom adesso? Omdat je bij ons écht kunt meebouwen.

Bij adesso Nederland draait het om meer dan alleen technologie. We bouwen slimme oplossingen die daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegen voor onze klanten. Geen eindeloze experimenten of AI omdat het hip is, maar technologie die werkt en impact maakt.

We zijn onderdeel van de internationale adesso Group, met ruim 11.500 collega's op meer dan 60 locaties. Tegelijkertijd zijn we in Nederland een relatief klein en persoonlijk team, met korte lijnen, veel vrijheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief.

Groot genoeg om impact te maken, klein genoeg om het verschil te voelen.

AI First: samen bouwen aan de toekomst

Bij adesso Nederland ontwikkelen we ons tot een AI First-organisatie. We geloven dat AI de manier waarop we software ontwikkelen, met data werken en klanten helpen fundamenteel verandert.

Daarom kijken we verder dan losse AI-experimenten. We bouwen aan slimme dataplatformen, AI-first applicaties en agentic oplossingen die écht onderdeel worden van bedrijfsprocessen.

Dat betekent ook dat we onze eigen manier van werken blijven vernieuwen. We omarmen nieuwe technologie, maar blijven kritisch: niet alles hoeft met AI. De beste oplossing staat altijd voorop.

 
En misschien wel het belangrijkste: de mensen

We houden van collega's die nieuwsgierig zijn, kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Mensen die goed zijn in hun vak, maar ook plezier hebben in samenwerken. Je krijgt bij ons vertrouwen, verantwoordelijkheid en de vrijheid om ideeën daadwerkelijk uit te voeren.

Wat krijg je van ons?

  • Een salaris van €4.500,- tot €5.750,- afhankelijk van jouw kennis en ervaring;

  • 8% vakantiegeld;

  • Contract voor 32 tot 40 uur per week;

  • Een leaseauto of mobiliteitsvergoeding boven op je salaris;

  • 27 vakantiedagen en 4 studiedagen;

  • €3.600 persoonlijk ontwikkelbudget per jaar en ruimte voor certificeringen;

  • Hybride werken met flexibele werktijden;

  • Goede pensioenregeling;

  • Doorgroeimogelijkheden;

  • Internationale kennis en ontwikkelmogelijkheden, gecombineerd met een hecht Nederlands team.

Binnen de eerste zes maanden heb je de belangrijkste Rechtshulp-processen geanalyseerd en vertaald naar bruikbare requirements voor Dynamics.

Onze werkplek is sterk gebaseerd op Microsoft 365, maar omvat meer dan alleen de digitale werkplek. Denk ook aan randapparatuur, lokale ondersteuning en supportdienstverlening. Je hoeft niet zelf de technisch specialist te zijn. Wel begrijp je moderne werkplekdienstverlening voldoende om een stevige gesprekspartner te zijn voor engineers, architecten, securityspecialisten en leveranciers.

 
Een belangrijk onderdeel van je rol is de operationele samenwerking met onze externe servicedesk en andere leveranciers. Samen met het team geef je richting aan prioriteiten en verbeteringen en zorg je dat ontwikkelingen binnen Werkplek & Support goed aansluiten op de ondersteuning van onze medewerkers.


Je voelt je daarnaast thuis in een omgeving die verandert. Je durft bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie te stellen, kunt omgaan met weerstand en neemt stakeholders mee wanneer nog niet alles vaststaat.

Wat ga je doen

Je kunt verschillende belangen afwegen en duidelijke besluiten nemen en onderbouwen;
•    Je kunt vanuit een Product Owner-rol richting en focus geven aan een team zonder formeel leidinggevende te zijn;

•    Je begrijpt werkplekdienstverlening en IT om inhoudelijk een stevige gesprekspartner te zijn;
•    Je hebt ervaring met het verbeteren van dienstverlening en kunt sturen op snelheid, voorspelbaarheid en klantbeleving;
•    Je kunt omgaan met weerstand, bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie stellen en koers houden wanneer nog niet alles duidelijk is;

Elke dag checken 6,5 miljoen Nederlanders in om te reizen met het OV. Met de OV-chipkaart, OV-pas, betaalpas, creditcard of mobiel. En dat werkt simpel en soepel. Kaart voor de lezer en … ‘bliep’. Je beweegt je gemakkelijk op senior niveau en voert gesprekken met zowel inhoudelijke experts als directies en bestuurders. Daarbij begrijp je niet alleen de commerciële kant van partnerships, maar ook hoe de paymentketen inhoudelijk werkt. Je weet wat ontwikkelingen binnen issuing, acquiring en card schemes betekenen voor Translink en kunt deze vertalen naar concrete keuzes en afspraken.

Intern werk je nauw samen met onder andere Product, Finance, Risk, Legal, Operations en IT. Daarnaast vorm je samen met collega’s die zich meer richten op ontwikkeling en data een sterk team: jij richt je primair op de externe relaties en strategische partnerships.

  • Je bouwt en onderhoudt strategische relaties met Visa, Mastercard, Nederlandse banken, issuers en andere relevante partijen binnen payments.

We zoeken een ervaren paymentprofessional die zijn of haar sporen in de sector heeft verdiend. Je begrijpt hoe banken, issuers, acquirers en card schemes met elkaar samenwerken en weet wat er nodig is om binnen dat complexe speelveld duurzame partnerships op te bouwen.

Je voelt je comfortabel aan tafel met senior stakeholders en bestuurders. Je kunt complexe onderwerpen helder uitleggen en weet de vertaalslag te maken tussen de buitenwereld en de interne organisatie. Tegelijkertijd ben je pragmatisch. Je bouwt niet alleen relaties, maar zorgt ook dat afspraken daadwerkelijk leiden tot resultaat.

Voor een ervaren professional biedt deze rol bovendien iets bijzonders: je werkt aan een maatschappelijk relevant betalingssysteem dat dagelijks door miljoenen reizigers wordt gebruikt.

  • Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar relevante werkervaring binnen payments, banking, fintech, strategic partnerships, business development of relatiemanagement.

  • Je hebt aantoonbare ervaring met partijen zoals card schemes, banken, issuers, acquirers, paymentnetwerken of andere organisaties binnen het betalingsverkeer.

  • Je hebt kennis van onderwerpen zoals scheme rules, scheme economics, fees, incentives en ontwikkelingen binnen het internationale betalingsverkeer.

  • Je bent gewend om complexe relaties en onderhandelingen op senior niveau te voeren.

  • Je kunt marktontwikkelingen, financiële belangen en inhoudelijke vraagstukken vertalen naar heldere voorstellen en concrete resultaten.

  • Je bent organisatiesensitief, analytisch en zelfstandig en weet mensen mee te krijgen zonder formele hiërarchie.

  • Je beheerst zowel het Nederlands als het Engels uitstekend.

WAT BIEDT TRANSLINK JOU?

Translink is een leuke, uitdagende werkplek. We werken in een dynamische, veelzijdige omgeving met een hoog ontwikkeltempo. Samenwerken, Wendbaarheid en Zelfregie zijn onze kernwaarden en dat proef je op de werkvloer.

Je kunt in goed overleg hybride werken en we bieden bewegingsruimte om balans aan te brengen tussen je werk- en privéleven. Zo kun je met onze thuiswerkregeling ook thuis een fijne werkplek inrichten.

Daar bovenop ontvang je een keuzebudget van 6,94% van je salaris, dit is gemiddeld € 500,- p/m. Daarnaast krijg je 8% vakantiegeld, reiskosten en een goede pensioenregeling. title: Tech Lead (Medical Coding Agents) (m/w/d)
description:
About Recare

As one of the leading German HealthTech companies, we are reshaping discharge management: technology-driven, patient-centered and free from bureaucracy. In addition to our market-leading SaaS platform, we develop AI solutions that radically simplify processes in hospitals and for aftercare providers, relieve healthcare professionals and refocus attention on patients. Today, we already connect two-thirds of all German hospitals with thousands of rehabilitation clinics, nursing and homecare providers. With around 100 employees, we continue to grow, and we’re looking for people with character who want to help us improve the healthcare system.


What you’ll do as our Tech Lead (Medical Coding Agents) (m/w/d):

German hospitals are paid a fixed amount per case, based on the codes assigned to it. Insurers dispute a share of the bills through an external medical audit, and the hospital can appeal when the audit cuts a bill. Recare is building medical coding agents to rebuild this chain: they read the case file, propose codes, assess audit findings and draft appeals. A subject matter expert reviews every result.

You’ll lead the technical development of this product. The role is about 80% hands-on building and 20% leading, and it grows with the platform into areas beyond billing.


  • Technical direction: set the architecture with the team across backend, frontend and a data model built on healthcare standards such as FHIR. Set the technical roadmap with the team and deliver on it predictably.

  • Agent orchestration: design how models, deterministic rules and human review fit together. Work with our AI engineers on system design.

  • Hands-on delivery: build the backend for cases, documents and long-running agent runs, including the append-only decision log that keeps every case audit-proof when an insurer challenges it months later.

  • Product partnership: be the technical counterpart to the product manager and the subject matter experts on planning, specs and trade-offs.

  • Production quality: own reliability, observability and security in a sensitive healthcare context, with an eval harness built from expert-reviewed cases as a CI gate.

How we work:

  • AI coding agents: engineers use them every day and take responsibility for the code we ship. Product managers and designers prototype in our codebase too, and engineers review what goes to production.

  • Human-in-the-loop: agents propose, the expert accepts, corrects or rejects, and every decision is logged with its evidence.

  • Shipping: we release early to development partners and switch features on per hospital.

  • Data protection: EU-only inference and no patient data in logs are hard constraints.

  • Ownership: product owns what we build and why. The tech lead owns how it’s built and that it ships.

  • Stack: TypeScript, Node.js and Go, Python for inference, Postgres, React, AWS Bedrock, Docker and Datadog.

  • Success: measured in revenue hospitals keep, not in usage.



What we’re looking for:

  • Leadership: 6+ years of experience, including leading a small team.

  • Hands-on with LLMs: you’ve built with LLMs yourself and understand where they fail: non-determinism, cost, latency and evaluation. You can design systems around them and challenge our AI engineers’ choices. Experience running an LLM or agent system in production is a strong plus, and strong personal projects count.

  • Evals: you can answer “how did you know it was good enough?” with ground truth, regression tests and a clear taxonomy of error classes.

  • Full-stack depth: you go deep across backend, frontend and data, and you commit code.

  • Other people’s systems: you’re comfortable with asynchronous pipelines, legacy interfaces and code written by others. Hospital experience isn’t required.

  • Communication: you explain decisions and trade-offs clearly in English in a remote team.

  • Nice to have: German, as the catalogues, the coding rules and much of the work with our experts are in German; an ML background, including judgement on when fine-tuning pays off; retrieval and source attribution; healthcare data standards such as FHIR; regulation such as MDR and the EU AI Act.

What we offer

  • Growth: we invest in each person’s development, whether that’s taking ownership of new projects, deepening your technical leadership or exploring new AI approaches, supported by a dedicated learning and development budget and regular feedback. If you grow, we grow.

  • Purposeful work: your work has a real impact on patients, their families and healthcare professionals.

  • Company culture: flat hierarchies, strong team dynamics and a culture of mutual respect, loyalty and recognition. English is our working language across a team of 20+ nationalities.

  • Flexibility: need to pick up your child from daycare or want to exercise at lunch? We support you, with fully remote work, flexible hours and workations by arrangement.

  • Your setup: a work laptop plus a one-off budget to choose and keep your own accessories.

  • Monthly benefit: €50 per month for vouchers or an Urban Sports Club membership (for employees in Germany).

  • Birthday off: your birthday off to celebrate with your loved ones.

  • Together: team meetups and company-wide events.

Location

We’re a remote team, and the role is fully remote within European time zones. We’re hiring in Germany, Austria, Spain, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.
