Founding engineer: AI that reads mechanical designs (Berlin / remote EU):

LoopforgeLab enables machine and hardware makers make better design decisions by better we mean shorter design iterations, more sustainable products with less cost to manfuacture and own.

We are building the Forge Engine is an agentic tool for manufacturing. Give it a BOM and a STEP file and it returns what the part costs to make and what the machine will cost to own over fifteen years, while there is still time to change the design. The lifecycle engine is built and runs on declared drivers. The agent already modifies geometry from natural-language instructions on our platform.

The next piece is the reason we are hiring. What you would own:

You'll own organic discoverability for Lovable. Answer engines come first, on top of a strong foundation in traditional search. You do the strategy, building and measurement, there's no queue between an insight and a live change.

title: Product Support Engineer - EMEA
description:
Hello!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Product Support Engineer in EMEA 🎉

We’re expanding our global Support team to provide 24/7 coverage across time zones. You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in EMEA, with the ownership and visibility that come from being one of the first Support Engineers across European time zones. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process.

Not sure which Support role is right for you?

We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles.

  • Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

  • Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review.

About the role

Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As an early Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team.

What you’ll own

  • Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation—investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved.

  • Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues.

  • Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers.

  • Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement.

  • Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

  • Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence.

You should apply if:

  • You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior.

  • You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes.

  • You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones.

  • You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design.

  • You want to be an early technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team.

You should not apply if:

  • You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership.

  • Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deployment—and you haven’t worked extensively with customer-centric SaaS applications, APIs, logs, or data-backed troubleshooting.

  • You prefer to pass difficult issues to another team rather than reproduce, investigate, and explain them yourself.

  • You’re looking for a role focused mainly on writing production code; this role diagnoses and escalates bugs but does not own code changes.

  • You prefer clear-cut problems and predefined answers over working through ambiguity with careful documentation, focused questions, and evidence-based decisions.

  • You want a narrowly defined role without regional operating ownership or projects that improve how the broader Support team works.

About Ashby

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com.

About Go To Market

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.

Interview process

Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical reasoning, communication precision, and ownership.

  • Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min

  • Take-home assessment — 5 days to complete

  • Hiring Manager interview — 45–60 min

  • Virtual onsite — 120 min

    • Meet the team — 30 min

    • Technical & integration skills — 45 min

    • CS and Support leadership — 30 min

    • Closing questions — 15 min

Onboarding

Your onboarding will combine Ashby-wide product and company training with a Support Engineering-specific ramp plan. You’ll learn the product and support workflow, get familiar with the tools and systems used for technical investigations, and build relationships across Support, Product, and Engineering. With support from your manager and onboarding buddy, you’ll take on increasingly complex investigations as you build context, with regular check-ins throughout your first 90 days.

Benefits

Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget.

  • A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop.

  • Opportunities to spend time with teammates through an annual company offsite, team offsites, local meetups, and virtual events.

  • Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record)

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

 

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

 

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

 

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

 

The Role

BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

 

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.

 

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

 

What you'll be doing

  • Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

  • Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

  • Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

  • Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

  • Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

  • Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

  • Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

     

What you'll need

  • Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

  • Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  • Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

  • AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

  • Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

     

Outcomes

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

     

Location

This role is based in UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 
 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

 

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

across regions. 

Most of our programs are funded by corporate partners who expect measurable impact. 

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in program management, team leadership, stakeholder engagement, acceleration and incubation programs, making sure every program changes founders’ trajectories.

You will report to the VP of Global Operations and be part of INCO’s operational leadership team.

What you’ll do:

Strategy and portfolio leadership

  • Define and own the multi year strategy for INCO Entrepreneurs:  which founders we serve, what we prioritise and how we stand out in the entrepreneurship support ecosystem.

  • Manage the program portfolio: launch, scale, redesign based on impact data, funder demand and ecosystem gaps.

  • Spot market gaps and new models, such as sector-specific accelerators, investment-readiness tracks and hybrid or online formats, where INCO Entrepreneurs can add distinctive value.

  • Build strong links with INCO Ventures (deal-flow pipeline, investment readiness), INCO Spaces (physical hubs for founders) and INCO Academy.

Growth, funders and business development

  • Own the total of the entrepreneurship portfolio’s budget

  • Lead the senior relationship with key funders. Set expectations,support contract negotiations and renewals, and find opportunities to expand.

  • Support proposal strategy and collaborate with the partnerships team, so every commitment can be delivered and is financially sound.

  • Represent INCO Entrepreneurs externally at ecosystem events with investors, public bodies and in the media as a credible voice on inclusive entrepreneurship.

Impact and quality

  • Set the impact framework and headline KPIs, such as founder revenue growth, funding raised, jobs created, business survival and founder diversity.

  • Make sure monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) results feed into program design decisions and into persuasive impact stories for funders.

  • Hold the unit to high standards in founder experience, mentor and expert quality, and program outcomes.

Leadership and team

  • Lead and develop the team’s leadership.

  • Shape team structure and staffing plans in line with the funder pipeline and budget. Lead senior hiring.

  • Build a high-performance, collaborative and inclusive culture across regions and time zones, with clear goals, regular feedback and real room to grow.

  • Coach the Associate Director as a potential future Director.

Financial management

  • Own the entrepreneurship portfolio P&L: budgeting, forecasting, margin and cost per founder supported.

  • Allocate resources across programs maximising our impact on the ground.

Your mission

At Doctolib, we're building digital health solutions used by more than 90 million patients and 520,000 healthcare professionals across Europe. The quality, consistency, and accessibility of our interfaces are critical to that mission. That's exactly what our Design System team makes possible.

As Engineering Manager of the Design System team, you will lead the engineering efforts behind Oxygen, Doctolib's design system. Oxygen goes far beyond a component library: it is the infrastructure that ensures design quality at scale and delivers our brand identity consistently across an AI-first development environment. With over 50 designers and several hundred engineers building across multiple markets and product surfaces, your work directly shapes the experience of every user who interacts with Doctolib.

Working at the intersection of Design and Engineering, you will partner with designers, product managers, and engineers to turn our Design System vision into scalable technical solutions that power consistent, high-quality user interfaces across all Doctolib products.

  • Champion an AI-first approach, exploring and scaling AI-powered tools and workflows that help designers and engineers build high-quality user interfaces more efficiently.

  • Establish and promote UI and accessibility engineering best practices, working closely with designers, product teams, and our accessibility specialist to drive adoption across the organization.

  • High ownership: own the full feasibility stack end to end, as the CEO of that part.

Team

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He's a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we're a team of 12: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise.

We're small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.

Why We'll Win

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design Yet

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability; parametric tools only check constraints after generation, leading to designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this, but doesn't yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.

title: Change and Transformation Manager - Client Delivery (Fluency in French & English required)
description:
Change and Transformation Manager – Client Delivery (French/english)

Location: Paris, France (hybrid, three days a week in the office; occasional travel to Brussels and London)
Level: Programme Manager senior
Team: Client Delivery
Contract: Permanent
Reporting To: Operating Model Design Lead

Please note: This role is based in France, so you need to live here or be open to relocating, and it requires an existing right to work in the EU. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

Fluent French and English (spoken and written) are essential, and we kindly ask you to submit your CV in English.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do

  • Own change and transformation support for go-live readiness for ENGIE France’s migration onto Kaluza as the hands-on lead, from planning through cutover, hypercare and transition towards scaling, so ENGIE’s teams are ready and confident to adopt the platform from day one.

  • Decide the change approach for the programme: stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, training design and business readiness engagement, shaped to ENGIE France’s operating context and owned by their teams.

  • Operate Kaluza’s business readiness governance: stage gates, readiness evidence, risk and dependency tracking and weekly reporting.

  • Partner with the Learning and Adoption Specialist in France to coordinate training, Train the Trainer and knowledge content, so enablement lands throughout each programme increment as we build out and release features via Agile delivery.

  • Be the day-to-day point of contact for ENGIE France on business readiness, change and adoption, giving practical change advice to their transformation leads.

  • Track adoption and operational stability through hypercare, root-cause any shortfall against acceptance criteria, and agree interventions with ENGIE.

  • Improve Kaluza’s readiness playbook: evolve what worked on ENGIE Belgium, test fixes where it falls short in France, and share what you learn with colleagues across Client Delivery to shape the platform’s operational foundations and improvements and to set our global standards.

Day to day, the activities you’ll lead or support include:

  • Change impact and readiness planning: diagnosing the full scope of impacts across roles, workflows, systems and customer experience, then turning them into a prioritised readiness plan sequenced against delivery, migration and release cadence.

  • Stakeholders, sponsors and change networks: mapping stakeholders and influence at workstream level, helping sponsors stay visible and engaged, and shaping the champion, superuser and people-manager networks that carry change into ENGIE’s business.

  • Communications and resistance: supporting ENGIE France’s own communications and engagement strategy, so their teams and customers hear a consistent, positive story about the programme. You’ll help leaders and champions advocate for the change, internally and with customers, and anticipate where resistance may form so you can intervene before it becomes entrenched.

  • Migration and go-live readiness: building the business and operational readiness evidence that enables a smooth transfer to service, measured against the agreed acceptance criteria, and supporting the go-live command centre.

  • Hypercare and stabilisation: agreeing hypercare entry and exit criteria, monitoring stability and adoption signals, and handing over cleanly to ENGIE’s business-as-usual teams.

  • Early releases and workarounds: planning for known limitations in early releases, and reflecting them in training, knowledge and communications so users are never caught by surprise. You’ll work with Release Management so each platform release arrives with the enablement it needs.

What you’ll bring

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Several years of hands-on change delivery on large platform or systems transformations, with a recognised change management discipline. You solve a wide range of problems creatively and work with little supervision.

  • Experience in regulated, customer-facing operational environments, including live customer account migration, cutover and go-live, where you have shaped the approach rather than only followed one.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management, credible with client programme leads and transformation sponsors.

  • Fluency in French and English, written and spoken.

  • Comfort working with data: you explore adoption and programme data yourself, report on it clearly and challenge decisions when evidence is weak.

  • Commercial awareness: you understand how Kaluza makes money and balance what the client needs against cost, working alongside SI partners and the client’s own change resources without duplicating effort.

What will set you apart: a background in energy retail or utilities, vendor-side experience on a SaaS implementation, and/or knowledge of contact centre operations and technology.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Financial & Insurance: Discretionary bonus, Alan Mutuelle Health Insurance, x3 Life & Death insurance (Prévoyance) via Alan, and standard Sécurité Sociale contributions (pension, family allowance, unemployment insurance)

  • Allowances: 50% commuting expense reimbursement, €200 Home Working Allowance, and €150 Learning Fund

  • Time Off & Flexibility: 25 days holiday + bank holidays + RTT days, Moments That Matter Leave, Compassionate Leave, two paid Volunteering Days, Flexible Working, and Career Break eligibility

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

Das bringst du mit:

Wir sind LIQID, einer der führenden digitalen Vermögensverwalter in Europa und eines der am schnellsten wachsenden deutschen Fintechs. title: Enterprise Customer Success Team Lead DACH
description:
SoSafe has the ambition to become the leading human risk management provider in Europe. Our award-winning awareness platform triggers behavioural change by providing effective and engaging training and simulations on cybersecurity and data protection. Cybercrime is predicted to cost the world $10.5 trillion annually by 2025 - we invite you to be part of the solution!

Are you a people-person who thrives on helping others grow and succeed? Do you enjoy coaching, sharing your knowledge, and setting your peers up for success? This newly created role offers the opportunity to build our first Enterprise focused Customer Success team for DACH. • Lead, guide, and support a team of Enterprise Customer Success Managers, driving performance against key metrics (gross retention, net revenue retention, and expansion) across a portfolio of high-value, strategic accounts
• Build and own the enterprise account strategy including risk management, expansion planning, and executive sponsorship programs for your team's book of business
• Coach your team on navigating complex, multi-stakeholder buying and renewal environments, including negotiation strategy and commercial structuring for high-ARR contracts
• Personally engage with C-level and senior stakeholders on strategic accounts to build executive relationships, resolve escalations, and reinforce long-term partnership value
• Clearly communicate company vision, strategy, and goals within your team, translating them into account-level execution

• Spot knowledge gaps and training needs, setting your team up for success while identifying process and tooling improvements to scale enterprise-grade delivery
• Analyze account health data and portfolio trends to shape targeted strategies, risk mitigation plans, and expansion initiatives across the Enterprise segment
• Represent the voice of the enterprise customer internally, ensuring insights from strategic accounts inform product, process, and go-to-market decisions
• Cultivate advocacy at the executive level references, case studies, and speaking opportunities turning strategic accounts into brand champions

What makes you a great fit:
• 10+ years Customer Success experience in a fast-growing B2B SaaS company, with meaningful time managing enterprise or strategic accounts
• 3+ years leading Enterprise Customer Success teams, ideally with exposure to complex or multi-stakeholder account portfolios
• Demonstrated ability to build relationships with and influence senior/C-level stakeholders, both externally and internally
• Commercial acumen, comfortable with quantifying ROI/value for large accounts
• Strong track record of retention and expansion within complex, multi-threaded accounts
• Naturally curious, skilled at uncovering stakeholders' goals, politics, and buying dynamics beyond the obvious
• Resilience and grit, able to stay effective and solution-oriented navigating escalations, ambiguity, and high-stakes conversations
• Confident communicator and presenter, capable of holding a room with senior internal and external stakeholders
• Empathetic and people-oriented, able to build trust-based relationships internally and externally while motivating and inspiring others
• Happy to travel ~30% of the time for customer onsites and industry events
• Fluent in English and German
• Based in Cologne or Berlin within a reasonable commute to our office

What we offer*

  • Work/Life balance: flexible hours, 33 vacation days

  • Wellbeing and Financial support: Open Up, Corporate Discounts

  • Coming together for moments that matter: annual company off-site, team events, local meet-ups

  • And the list goes on: Learning & Development Allowance, Tech Equipment, Referral Bonuses, Dog Friendly HQ



*Perks and Benefits listed above are for full-time employees and can vary slightly by office location. These are just a sample; you’ll learn about more benefits offered during the interview process

About Us
At SoSafe, we’re on a mission to make the digital world safer by addressing the human factor in cybersecurity. As one of the fastest-growing security awareness scale-ups worldwide, we leverage behavioural science and data-driven learning to empower people against cyber threats. Our Human Risk Management approach helps organisations turn their employees into their strongest line of defence.
Backed by leading VCs like Highland Europe and Global Founders Capital, we’re rapidly expanding across the globe. We’re looking for team players who want to drive meaningful change in cybersecurity, take ownership of their work, and grow with us.
If you thrive in a vibrant, purpose-driven environment that values innovation, diversity, and collaboration, then this is the place for you!

title: Branch Support Manager - Europe
description:
About Rain for Rent International

Rain for Rent International provides innovative tank systems for liquid management applications. As an internationally operating rental and service company, expertise centers on rental, logistics, and services around the tank, focusing on the core competencies of renting storage tanks, containment systems, pumps, and filtration units.

Your role

We are looking for a hands-on Branch Support Manager ( m/f/d ) to help our teams across Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and France get the best from our business systems, processes and support functions.

This is not a traditional IT Manager position.

It is a highly business-facing role combining business systems, operational processes, user support, training, continuous improvement and team leadership. You will work closely with our branches and Shared Services teams to understand how people work, where they encounter challenges and how technology and better processes can make their jobs easier and our business more effective.

What you will do

Become a Business Systems Expert

You will develop strong expertise in the applications supporting our European operations and become a trusted point of contact for our business users.

A major focus will be our ERP environment, supporting processes such as:

  • Purchasing and purchase orders

  • Goods and invoice receipt

  • Rental contracts

  • Equipment on-hire and off-hire

  • Recurring and final billing

  • Credit notes and ad-hoc invoicing

  • Customer, supplier and item master data

You will also support the effective use of CRM, Microsoft 365 and other operational applications.

Experience with inspHire, Zoho or Twinfield would be advantageous, but previous knowledge of our specific applications is not essential if you have strong ERP/business systems experience and learn quickly.

Help People Get the Best From Technology

You will work directly with colleagues across our branches to understand challenges, answer questions and identify better ways of working.

That includes:

  • Providing practical systems and process support

  • Training new and existing users

  • Developing SOPs, quick-reference guides and training materials

  • Creating screen recordings and short training videos

  • Building a structured, version-controlled knowledge library

  • Identifying recurring problems and addressing their root causes

Most importantly, you will explain the why, not only the how.

Connect Systems With Business Reality

Good systems only create good information when they are used correctly.

You will therefore work closely with Operations, Sales, Finance, Fleet and other Shared Services functions to improve the quality and consistency of the processes behind our data.

You will help us ensure that operational information, CRM pipelines, rental transactions, margins and management KPIs accurately reflect what is happening in the business.

Listen, Challenge and Improve

Our branches know their business and will bring you ideas and requirements.

Your job is not simply to say yes.

You will listen, understand the underlying need and assess whether the best answer is a change to a system, process, training or something else.

For larger initiatives, you will help structure requirements, assess benefits, costs, effort and risks, and make clear recommendations to leadership.

Lead a Small Team

You will lead a developing Branch Support function, expected to include approximately three team members across business support and IT/helpdesk activities.

This remains a hands-on role. You will lead the team while actively participating in support, training, problem solving and improvement initiatives yourself.

Stay Curious

Technology is changing quickly and we want to take advantage of it.

You do not need to be an AI expert, but you should be curious about tools such as Microsoft Copilot, automation and new ways technology can help colleagues work more effectively.

The Person We Are Looking For

Systems knowledge matters, but how you work with people matters just as much.

You are someone who:

  • Listens before proposing a solution

  • Is patient and enjoys explaining things

  • Can train and support colleagues with different levels of systems experience

  • Builds credibility and strong working relationships

  • Can persuade and influence without relying on hierarchy

  • Is comfortable constructively challenging a request

  • Is pragmatic and realistic about priorities, resources and costs

  • Learns new business processes quickly

  • Enjoys solving problems

  • Is comfortable being visible and close to the operational business

  • Is curious about technology and AI

You should be equally comfortable discussing a process with a branch administrator, working through a systems problem with IT, understanding a commercial requirement from Sales or presenting a recommendation to leadership.

European Scope

The role supports operations across Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and France.

Regular interaction with the branches is a fundamental part of the position. You should therefore be willing to travel across our European locations, build strong relationships with local teams and spend time understanding how our operations work in practice.

Regular office presence is also expected, currently anticipated at up to three days per week at our office in Potsdam.

Why This Role?

This is an opportunity to shape a developing European support function rather than simply inherit an established helpdesk.

You will have the opportunity to influence:

  • How we use our business systems

  • How we support and train users

  • How processes are standardised across countries

  • How knowledge is documented and shared

  • How new technology and AI are adopted

  • How Branch Support develops as our European organisation evolves

If you enjoy bringing together people, processes and technology and want a role where you can see the practical impact of your work across the business, we would like to hear from you.

Rain for Rent International is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive working environment and welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, disability, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
SENIOR DEVOPS ENGINEER

Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. We work with over 5,000+ teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes' health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.  

Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS

We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to help build, operate and improve the infrastructure, platforms and tools that enable our teams to develop, deliver and run reliable software at scale.

Based in Cologne, you will join a team with broad ownership of our technical environment. We take a cloud-agnostic approach, combining cloud services and self-hosted infrastructure to meet the needs of our products and engineering teams. Our responsibilities span the full lifecycle, from provisioning and deployment to observability, security and ongoing operation.

You will combine infrastructure expertise with automation and software engineering to improve how our software is built, deployed and operated. This includes streamlining development workflows, integrating and maintaining shared tools, and supporting demanding workloads across data processing, media and machine learning. Working closely with engineering teams and colleagues across the business, you will build practical solutions that support our expanding product portfolio.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving a wide range of technical problems, takes ownership from initial idea through to production, and thrives in a fast-growing environment where priorities and requirements evolve quickly. You will help shape how our infrastructure, platforms and tools adapt as the business grows.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Design, operate, and continuously improve our Kubernetes platform across both self-hosted clusters and AWS
  • Own our infrastructure as code using Terraform and Ansible, driving a GitOps workflow to ensure all changes are versioned, reviewed, and reproducible
  • Build and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI) and shared templates that empower product teams to build, test, and deploy reliably
  • Operate and scale specialized infrastructure for demanding workloads, including GPU clusters for computer vision models, media engines, and data analytics platforms 
  • Evolve our observability stack to proactively monitor system health, define meaningful alerting, and ensure high availability
  • Drive platform security and compliance through continuous vulnerability scanning, automated image screening, robust secrets management, and strict access controls
  • Collaborate closely with software engineers, data scientists, and product teams to design scalable architectures and act as a strategic technical partner for new infrastructure initiatives 

Help define technical direction, engineering best practices, and quality standards within the infrastructure domain 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 5+ years of professional experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Platform Engineering, with a proven track record of designing and scaling highly available production environments 
  • Strong hands-on experience running Kubernetes in production, including upgrades, networking and troubleshooting
  • Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure (AWS) combined with experience operating bare-metal or self-hosted environments

Proven experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) and modern container build or GitOps workflowsStrong problem-solving skills and the ability to evaluate technical trade-offs between reliability, scalability, and maintainabilityExperience collaborating across engineering and product teams to deliver secure and robust infrastructure solutionsDeep understanding of Linux operating systems and strong programming or scripting skills (e.g., Python, Go, or Bash) focused on automation and tooling. 

Nice to have – and what would make you exceptional:

  • Experience operating GPU workloads on Kubernetes or Machine Learning infrastructure
  • Familiarity with specialized Kubernetes ecosystem tools such as FluxCD, Rancher, or RKE2.
  • Experience working with large-scale video/streaming workflows or AWS media services
  • Experience managing and scaling messaging or event-streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) 
  • Experience operating and optimizing relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL) 
  • Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling for engineering teams

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • In 6 months time… You know our clusters and pipelines, handle incidents and upgrades on your own, and have shipped your first improvements to reliability, automation or security. You contribute confidently to architecture discussions.
  • In 12 months time… You own major parts of the platform, have delivered measurable improvements (faster deployments, better observability, stronger security), and help shape the roadmap of our hybrid cloud.

WHY CATAPULT? 

  • We have amazing people. We promise you'll work with some of the most ambitious,  intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
  • We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary. 
  • We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
  • Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.  
  • We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve.  There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

Whether you're interested in sports or not, you'll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet!

description:

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Senior Software Engineer, Event Streaming Systems

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our team. This is a hybrid role. In this role, you'll help us build and operate the event streaming infrastructure that powers business-critical workflows across Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt.

Get to know our Engineering team, what drives us, how we work, and what you can expect.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be joining the Event Streaming Systems team within the broader Storage organisation. The team builds and operates highly reliable, scalable and efficient event streaming infrastructure, including Kafka, Event Streaming abstractions(internally called EventBus) and future streaming platform technologies. These systems support Tier-0 workflows and are foundational to how engineering teams build reliable, event-driven products at scale.

Here's what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Design, build and operate large-scale event streaming infrastructure that supports critical production workloads.

  • Improve the reliability, scalability, observability and automation of Kafka, EventBus and related streaming platforms.

  • Debug complex distributed systems issues, including performance bottlenecks, capacity constraints and production reliability challenges.

  • Build infrastructure automation and self-healing capabilities that reduce operational toil and improve platform resilience.

  • Contribute to incident response, operational readiness and continuous improvement for Tier-0 infrastructure.

  • Partner closely with EventBus, Storage, SRE, Data Platform and Core Infrastructure teams across US and EU regions.

  • Help shape the long-term architecture and evolution of Deliveroo's event streaming platform.

What You'll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

  • Strong hands-on experience building or operating distributed systems in production.

  • Experience with Kafka or similar event streaming systems, either as a platform, infrastructure service or critical production dependency.

  • Strong coding ability in Java, Go, Python or similar languages, with a focus on reliable, maintainable production systems.

  • Experience operating scalable production infrastructure, including debugging, troubleshooting and improving reliability.

  • Strong understanding of infrastructure automation, observability, capacity management and operational excellence.

  • Good fundamentals in Linux, networking and JVM-based systems, or curiosity to deepen expertise in these areas.

  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across platform, infrastructure and product engineering teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience contributing to Kafka or related open source distributed systems.

  • Experience with Redpanda, WarpStream, AutoMQ, Pulsar or similar streaming technologies.

  • Experience with JVM tuning, broker tuning, partition management or Cruise Control.

  • Experience with tiered storage, diskless streaming architectures or multi-region event streaming platforms.

  • Experience operating Tier-0 infrastructure at large scale.

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving.

We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale
Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.

🌱 See your impact, fast
Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.

🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership

High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.

description:
Über YLAB

Wir bauen die KI, die wir unseren eigenen Kindern geben würden.

Kinder wachsen heute mit KI auf. Wir sorgen dafür, dass diese KI neugierig macht statt süchtig, sicher ist statt datenhungrig und für Kinder gebaut wird statt für Erwachsene.

Wir sind YLAB, ein kleines KI-Lab aus Köln-Ehrenfeld. Wir entwickeln Software und Hardware aus einer Hand, vom Sprachmodell bis zum Gehäuse. Warum YLAB

Deine Arbeit landet im Kinderzimmer, nicht in einem Dashboard.

Software & Hardware: KI, App, Firmware und Gerät entstehen bei uns zusammen. Du siehst, wie aus Code etwas wird, das ein Kind in die Hand nimmt.

Du arbeitest an echten offenen Fragen, zum Beispiel wie KI Kinderstimmen versteht und Fünfjährigen die Welt erklärt.

Tech, Pädagogik und Forschung sitzen bei uns an einem Tisch.

Ehrlichkeit statt Hochglanz: Vieles bauen wir zum ersten Mal. Wenn dich das reizt, sollten wir reden.

Was wir bieten

  • Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Du bekommst echte Themen und Probleme statt Tickets, und deine Entscheidungen haben Gewicht.

  • Top Arbeitsmaterial: Du arbeitest mit dem Setup und den Tools, die du brauchst.

  • Flexible Weiterbildung: Konferenz, Kurs oder Workshop – du sagst uns, was dich weiterbringt.

  • Hybrid mit Herz: Remote, wenn du Ruhe brauchst, und im Office, wenn wir gemeinsam tüfteln.

Über die Rolle

Wie versteht ein Sprachmodell eine Vierjährige? Und wie erklärt es ihr die Welt, ohne sie zu überfordern? Dazu gibt es kaum Paper und keine Benchmarks. Genau da setzt du an.

Du bist unsere erste dedizierte Research-Stelle. Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von KI, Sprache und Pädagogik, mit echten Familien statt Laborbedingungen und mit direktem Draht ins Produkt.

Was dich erwartet: offene Fragen mit Substanz, ein Fachbeirat aus Bildung und Psychologie und die Freiheit, Studien so zu bauen, wie sie sein müssen.

Wie du uns helfen kannst

  • Du entwirfst und machst Studien mit Kindern und Familien. Von der Beobachtung im Wohnzimmer bis zum strukturierten Test.

  • Du baust Methoden, um altersgerechte Antworten zu bewerten: Was heißt verständlich, was heißt zu viel?

  • Du übersetzt Erkenntnisse in Modell- und Produktentscheidungen, zusammen mit Engineering und Pädagogik.

  • Du behältst die Forschung im Blick (Child-Computer Interaction, Speech, LLM-Evals) und holst rein, was uns weiterbringt.

  • Du teilst, was wir lernen. Wir forschen nicht für die Schublade.

Melde dich, wenn:

  • Du hast einen Research-Hintergrund, etwa HCI, Psychologie, Linguistik oder ML.

  • Du hast schon mit Nutzer:innen geforscht, am besten mit Kindern.

  • Du kannst beides: Interviews auswerten und saubere Metriken bauen.

Eher nicht, wenn: du Forschung als Selbstzweck siehst oder zwei Jahre Vorlauf brauchst, bevor etwas testbar ist.

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. Our agentic engineering playbook is noticeably better because of you — you’ve added or rewritten the skills, rules, and AI review checks the team uses every day, and you lead by example in how you ship with agents.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager. You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 8+ years as a software engineer, including 4+ years managing a team of 8+ and hiring for it yourself

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You're an engineer at heart. You were senior or principal before you managed, and you can still hold your own in a design review, a debugging session, or building a feature

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • You've grown a team to 15+ at a VC-funded startup

  • Managed tech leads or a second manager

  • Previous experience at a fully remote company

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 60 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature.   • Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.

  • Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.

  • Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption.

title: RF Systems Engineer
description:

Loft Orbital is making space simple. We build and operate reliable, shareable satellites that give customers a faster, simpler path to orbit. By combining flight-proven spacecraft platforms with our own hardware and software, we make it easier to deploy missions in space.

As an RF Systems Engineer, you'll contribute to the design, development, and integration of communication systems across our satellite connectivity and next-generation RF payload programs. You'll work on RF system architecture, signal processing algorithms, and performance analysis, collaborating closely with FPGA, embedded software, systems, and hardware engineers to develop and integrate complex RF technologies.

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of RF hardware and signal processing, solving challenging technical problems, and seeing their work go from initial design to in-orbit operation.

  • Develop and optimize signal processing algorithms for RF payloads using MATLAB and related simulation tools.

  • Define and track system requirements, documenting technical decisions, integration activities, and verification results.

  • Knowledge of RF communication systems and subsystems, particularly S-band and X-band communications.

Loft’s Onboard Software group provides the on-orbit software that powers our satellite fleet — from the Linux services running on the Hub’s onboard computers, to the containerized workloads executing customer applications in low Earth orbit.

Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for an intern to join the End-to-End Validation & Performance (EVP) team and contribute to image-processing and calibration/validation (CAL/VAL) activities for Earth-observation missions. In this internship, you’ll explore how AIT captures and routine onboard imagery can support optical performance testing and radiometric calibration, and turn that work into an evaluated engineering prototype.

Location: Toulouse office, city center (Jeanne d’Arc metro station)
Duration: 6-month, end-of-studies internship — target start date: early 2027.


About this role:
  • Review DSNU, radiometric calibration, and relevant EVP processing and CAL/VAL practices.
  • Work with EVP engineers to identify suitable routine images, metadata, and reference calibration data; document data limitations and provenance.
  • Prepare a reproducible dataset and establish reference baselines, including a holdout evaluation strategy that avoids tuning and testing on the same acquisitions.
  • Implement a baseline estimator: a data-fit term combined with a regularizing prior.
  • Investigate additional AI/ML methods only where suitable training or validation data are available; compare them against the baseline rather than assuming they are superior.
  • Evaluate correction quality, residual fixed-pattern structure, stability across images, runtime, and failure cases.
  • Package the workflow as a prototype script or notebook with plots, quality checks, and an auditable record of inputs, parameters, and outputs.
  • Present findings and recommendations to EVP and CAL/VAL stakeholders; document what evidence would be needed before operational use.
    • The intern will gain experience in:
    • Radiometric calibration and CAL/VAL for space-based optical imaging.
    • Push-broom image characteristics and PRNU/DSNU correction.
    • Applied optimization and, where appropriate, machine learning for image processing.
    • Experimental design, reference-data limitations, and quantitative performance assessment.
    • Building reproducible engineering tools and communicating technical evidence to mission teams.

Must Haves:
  • Student in engineering, applied physics, remote sensing, image processing, data science, or a related field.
  • Fundamentals of signal or image processing and a strong interest in Earth observation.
  • Basic programming skills in Python and comfort working with scientific data.
  • Analytical mindset, rigor, and ability to document assumptions and limitations.
  • Interest in calibration, validation, sensor behavior, or image quality assessment.

Nice to Haves:
  • Exposure to satellite imagery or remote-sensing data.
  • Experience with optimization, statistical estimation, or machine-learning evaluation.
  • Familiarity with image-analysis libraries and scientific Python tools.
  • Understanding of radiometric calibration or data-quality assessment.

What Can We Offer?
You will join a stimulating environment, surrounded by passionate engineers, conducive to learning, innovation, and personal and professional development — and help build the future of space infrastructure. With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, USA | Golden, USA | and Toulouse, France.

title: AI/ML Engineering Intern: System 1 Models for Reactive Space Operations
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital flies other people's payloads on standardized satellites, giving our customers a fast, simple, and reliable path to orbit. Our AI for Space team is looking for a motivated intern to explore how fast, lightweight “System 1” models can boost reactivity, performance, and usability across our satellite operational chains.

Reactivity use cases are at the heart of Loft's vision, and we are scaling them: from single-satellite reactive loops, to two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue (a detection from one sensor automatically cueing an acquisition by another), and ultimately multi-satellite scenarios. Today we mostly rely on “System 2” models — powerful but slow and heavy at inference — from our partners. “System 1” models (fast, intuitive) are coming back strongly and could add value not only on reactivity, but also on performance and ease of use. This internship will assess that added value and prototype it on our reactivity scenarios.

Location: Toulouse office, city center (Jeanne d’Arc metro station)
Duration: 6-month, end-of-studies internship — target start date: early 2027.


About this role:
  • Review the state of the art on System 1 / fast, intuitive models and compare them with the System 2 models used today, including our partners' models.
  • Map where System 1 models could bring value in our operational chain for reactivity use cases, from detection to tasking.
  • Define benchmark scenarios of increasing complexity with the team: a single-satellite reactive loop, then a two-satellite / two-sensor tip & cue loop, and, as a stretch goal, a multi-satellite scenario.
  • Set the latency budget, accuracy needs, and execution context for each scenario.
  • Build datasets and evaluation sets from Loft data, partner outputs, and open datasets.
  • Train or fine-tune System 1 models and benchmark them against System 2 baselines on reactivity (latency), performance (accuracy, compute footprint), and ease of use (integration and operational effort).
  • Prototype an end-to-end reactive loop, possibly as a hybrid design where System 1 triggers and System 2 validates, and assess how it extends to multi-satellite coordination.
  • Document results and recommendations for production use, and deliver a final demo.

Must Haves:
  • Final-year engineering or Master's student specialized in ML / deep learning / computer vision.
  • Solid Python and PyTorch skills, and good software engineering practices.
  • Strong understanding of the state of the art in LLM / VLM / Reinforcement Learning.
  • Practical experience training neural networks (language models or computer vision) and/or LLM manipulation.

Nice to Haves:
  • Model optimization (quantization, distillation, edge inference).
  • Exposure to satellite or geospatial data.
  • Multi-agent or distributed systems experience.
  • Genuine interest in space.

What Can We Offer?
You will join the AI for Space team and directly support the scaling of reactivity use cases, a core part of Loft's vision — working toward shorter detection-to-tasking latency on single-satellite and tip & cue scenarios, and a first step towards multi-satellite reactive operations. You'll build new expertise on an emerging class of models, reusable across other detection-like use cases, with a concrete prototype and benchmark the team can build on.
