description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons une Post-doctorante ou un Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux pour rejoindre le département COMELEC à Télécom Paris.

Les fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers, HCPCF) ont récemment franchi une étape technologique majeure, avec des pertes de propagation pouvant atteindre 0.1 dB/km à 1550 nm, comparables, voire inférieures, à celles des fibres télécoms standards [1–2]. La lumière se propageant principalement dans l’air, les HCPCF présentent une latence réduite de 30 à 40 %, une dispersion ultra-faible et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables. Ces propriétés uniques en font des technologies particulièrement prometteuses pour les systèmes de télécommunications de nouvelle génération, la distribution quantique de clés (Quantum Key Distribution, QKD) sur longue distance et les applications de détection distribuée.

Le projet proposé vise à développer et démontrer la prochaine génération de fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (HCPCF) pour la transmission de données à haut débit et les applications de détection. La propagation de la lumière dans l’air plutôt que dans le verre permet aux HCPCF d’offrir une latence réduite et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables par rapport aux fibres de silice, répondant ainsi à certains des enjeux majeurs des futurs centres de données et réseaux optiques. Notre ambition est de démontrer une transmission à 400 Gbit/s sur quelques kilomètres à travers des échantillons de fibres issus de nouvelles architectures, et d’étudier le potentiel de ces HCPCF pour des applications de détection. La réalisation de ces objectifs nécessite de répondre à des spécifications exigeantes en matière de guidage monomode, de contrôle de la polarisation, ainsi que de faibles pertes par courbure et par couplage.

Deux équipes complémentaires assureront conjointement l'encadrement de ces travaux : le GPPMM, reconnu internationalement pour ses activités de conception et de fabrication de HCPCF [3–5], et le GTO, leader dans la démonstration de systèmes de communication optique et de détection à haut débit [6–8]. Un processus itératif entre la fabrication des fibres et leur caractérisation au niveau système permettra de s'assurer que leurs propriétés répondent aux exigences opérationnelles en matière de transmission et de détection. Sur le plan méthodologique, le projet combinera modélisation numérique, caractérisation et validation expérimentale dans la bande C. Les méthodes de modélisation et de traitement du signal développées au GTO pour le suivi de la polarisation contribueront à évaluer et à optimiser les performances de transmission des HCPCF conçues et caractérisées au GPPMM.

À propos du projet PLEIADES

Le projet PLEIADES s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme PEPR « Réseaux du futur », financé par l'ANR, et réunit un consortium de 14 partenaires. L'un des axes de travail porte sur les fibres à cœur creux de nouvelle génération et rassemble plusieurs laboratoires académiques, notamment LTCI, XLIM et PHLAM.

Vos principales missions seront de :

  • Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine de la photonique

  • Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Participer à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris


Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat ou équivalent en génie électrique, communications, photonique, traitement du signal ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez de solides connaissances en systèmes et réseaux de transmission optique ainsi qu’en traitement numérique du signal (DSP) appliqué aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique. La maîtrise de MATLAB et/ou Python pour le développement d’algorithmes DSP sera appréciée. Vous manifestez un intérêt marqué pour la recherche appliquée et êtes à l’aise dans un environnement multiculturel, notamment pour encadrer des stagiaires et/ou des étudiants. Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais est indispensable. Vous disposez également de bonnes qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, d’un bon esprit d’équipe et d’une capacité à synthétiser et à communiquer des informations complexes.

description:
🤓 About Luminovo

At Luminovo, we’re building the infrastructure that turns the electronics supply chain into something software can read and act on. Our customers use it to quote PCBAs faster, find cost savings and act on risks in their supply chain.

We serve 300+ customers, from Europe’s largest EMS to category-leading OEMs, with around 100 Luminerds across Munich, Berlin, New York and Austin. We’re backed by Chalfen Ventures, Cherry Ventures and General Catalyst. With data centers and robotics driving demand for electronics, someone needs to manage that supply chain, and they’ll need good software to do it. (Here’s why we care so much about electronics.)

🚀 Your role

Team Core is our platform team. Its job is to make all our other engineering teams more productive and to improve our codebase and infrastructure as a whole. You’ll:

  • Keep our DevOps setup and CI/CD pipelines fast and reliable

  • Build tools every team needs (e.g. interface for building permissions)

  • Act as an in-house Rust expert: our backend is a Rust monolith, and Team Core helps the other teams use good Rust patterns and architecture

  • Be responsible for the Developer Experience (DX).

  • Help our engineers use agents more productively

Other details

  • Location: remote-first, within two hours of CET. We prefer Munich > Berlin > Germany > Europe.

  • Tech stack: Rust, TypeScript + React, Postgres, Clickhouse, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, Helm, Flux

  • 🇺🇸 Some of the work in this role falls under US export control regulations (ITAR), so you must be a US citizen. You’ll need to be based in Europe, and if you’re currently in the US, we’ll support your relocation to Germany.

🖲️ Our tech stack

We always try to use the best tools available for the job. Don't worry, we don't need you to be familiar with all of these:

  • Main monolith is written in Rust (using actix-web as our web framework), deployed on Kubernetes

  • React and Typescript for frontend

  • PostgreSQL for persisting our data

  • Redis for caching and queues

  • Flux for GitOps

  • Honeycomb, Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring and observability

  • garden-io for developing on Kubernetes

  • Azure and Cloudflare for cloud computing

🤓 Whom you’ll be working with

  • Timon, one of our Founders

  • Alex and Tomas, two of our Staff Engineers

  • Inga, Senior Software Engineer

⚡️ Skills, knowledge, and expertise

Just so you know – we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. We care much more about your motivation and ability to help us accelerate technical progress than we care just about your CV. If you're interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles – see here.

⚡️ About Luminovo

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry.

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress.

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain.

To date, over 300 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million.

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things

As a remote-first company headquartered in Munich, our brilliant team is spread across cities including Munich, New York, Austin, Calgary, Berlin, London, Valencia, Nairobi, and Verona, among others. 🌍

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. Among us are graduates from institutions like Stanford University and the University of Cambridge, as well as talented individuals with unconventional CVs. What matters most is their drive to build great things.

We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

Build something that truly matters

At Cortea, we envision a world where every audit is proactively managed by humans and AI agents collaboratively. Where auditing professionals have superhuman capabilities at their fingertips to strengthen the trust in the world's most critical systems.

We're not just improving auditing workflows, we're redefining how audits are done from the ground up. With a rapidly growing, global customer base and backing from world-class investors, the market is ready. What we ship next decides how big this gets.

This is your chance to join a team of sharp, ambitious and kind builders extremely early. Shape the company at its pivotal moment and build something that truly matters.

About the role

At Cortea, design earns trust, and we sell to an industry that exists to produce it. Auditors are paid to be skeptical, and people judge quality by what they can see: the product, the website, the deck a partner opens in a boardroom, the newsletter someone reads with their first coffee. All of it is Cortea.

This is a role for someone with great taste in designing software and AI systems. You'll find novel patterns for problems that haven't existed in software before, and you'll own how Cortea looks and feels to the outside world.

Roughly 70% product, 30% brand. The product work is deep, expert-facing and systems-heavy. As we are doubling down on design, you'll be working on taking the core flows to the next level. The brand work is yours to own outright: website, marketing and sales visuals, newsletter, event and content assets. It'll be on screen in a Big4 boardroom, in every customer's inbox, and on the wall at the events we host. A lot of surface for one designer, and all of it yours.

We're not looking for someone to ask whether the logo goes left or right. We're looking for someone with opinions.

What you'll do

  • Work directly with our founders, engineers, and customers to turn audit flows into intuitive, delightful interfaces

  • Work with Jonas on product design and design strategy overall

  • Own our brand designs and visuals

  • Evolve our visual identity and design system

  • Take increasing ownership of brand direction. Website, marketing and sales material, content and event assets

  • Help shape the product vision, roadmap, and user experience standards

  • Run usability tests, build user feedback loops, and bring a systems mindset to design decisions

You'll be great at this if you

  • Have product design experience in B2B / SaaS, ideally in fast-moving startups.

  • Think in experiences, not screens. With taste you can defend. Product and brand are one surface; you can explain why details work, and you call out when they don’t.

  • Want to create a unique brand, which auditors love. Identify, marketing, web should be a draw, not a tax. Taste and passion matter more than volume.

  • Can hold complexity without losing clarity. You turn configuration-heavy, expert workflows into clear systems.

  • Use AI without sacrificing quality. You've worked out which parts of the job benefit from automation and which need your judgment.

  • Work well in ambiguity. You take rough direction and deliver great work without handholding.

  • Have low ego. Best idea wins. You give and take feedback without making it about you.

What you will get

  • Full brand ownership, shape how the product feels. Work face-to-face with experienced founders and learn directly from customer insights.

  • Fast, ambitious, and fun team. Decisions get made in hours, not weeks. Rapid experimentation is the default.

  • Meaningful equity and competitive salary. You are one of the first to build this, and you share in the upside.

  • A mission that matters. Building intelligent systems for a $200bn industry from Berlin, with AI at the core

Interview process

  • First Call — Intro on what we do with Liza

  • Second Call — Portfolio walkthrough with Jonas

  • Third Call — Get to know our product and culture with our Co-Founder Valentin

  • On-site Day — Meet our full team in our Berlin office and work on a real problem together with us.

title: Senior Technical Product Manager - Compliance & Recording
description:
About Us

1GLOBAL is a technology-driven global mobile communications provider helping enterprises and consumer brands deliver seamless connectivity worldwide. Powered by a best-in-class telecom platform, proprietary eSIM technology, and its own mobile core network across 15 countries, 1GLOBAL operates as a fully regulated telecommunications provider in 43 countries.


Founded in 2022, 1GLOBAL has rapidly become one of Europe's fastest-growing telecom technology companies, connecting more than 80 million people and devices globally. Our customers include leading banks, multinational enterprises, global retailers, travel companies, payment service providers, and digital-first businesses.


Headquartered in the Netherlands, with R&D hubs in Lisbon, Berlin, and São Paulo, 1GLOBAL employs over 550 professionals across 16 countries. With annual revenues exceeding US$200 million and a strong track record of profitability, we continue to invest in innovation, infrastructure, and international expansion as we redefine the future of global mobile connectivity.

About the Team

The Compliance & Recording team owns 1GLOBAL's products for regulated enterprises. We capture mobile voice, SMS and data at network level, with no app on the device, and deliver it to wherever our customers need it: their own on-site recorders and archives, or our Cloud Compliance service built on Verint Financial Compliance. On top of the recordings we offer Communications Analytics, which brings AI transcription, summaries and risk insights to compliance teams.

Our customers include 8 of the world's 10 largest banks. They rely on us for a complete, auditable record of every regulated call and message, so reliability and precision are at the heart of everything the team builds. We work closely with engineering, network, security, service delivery and commercial teams.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Product Manager to own how recorded communications are captured, delivered and analysed. This is an API-first, backend role: there is little UI at its core, because for our customers the integration is the product.

About the Role

You will lead product strategy and delivery for Compliance & Recording, from the APIs and delivery channels that move recorded data into customer environments to the AI capabilities we build on top of it. 

  • Own the vision, roadmap and backlog for Compliance & Recording, covering customer-managed (on-site) recording, Cloud Compliance and the integrations that connect them to customer systems.
  • Define and evolve how recorded voice, SMS and data reach customers through APIs, SFTP, SMTP and S3 bucket pushes, choosing the right mechanism for each use case.
  • Write precise technical requirements: API contracts, payload and metadata schemas, delivery guarantees, retry and failure handling, security controls and acceptance criteria.
  • Lead large projects for our biggest compliance customers, onboarding their engineering and compliance teams with proper documentation, from scoping through rollout.
  • Define and track success metrics such as delivery success rate, latency, capture completeness and time to integrate, and keep the roadmap aligned with regulatory change and the competitive landscape.

Requirements

About You

Must Have

  • 6+ years in product management, with end-to-end ownership of API-first, backend or platform products where there is little or no UI.
  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of APIs: REST design, authentication, versioning, webhooks, pagination, error handling and idempotency. You read OpenAPI specs, test endpoints yourself and hold your own in design discussions with engineers.
  • Solid understanding of file and message-based integrations such as SFTP, SMTP and object storage (for example AWS S3), including batch versus near real-time delivery, encryption and access control.
  • A track record of leading large, cross-functional projects for enterprise customers with demanding technical, security and reliability requirements.
  • Clear, precise writing: requirements, acceptance criteria and edge cases that engineering teams can build from without guesswork.
  • A genuine interest in compliance products and enterprise integrations. You want to understand how regulated firms capture, retain and supervise communications, and why every record matters.
  • Confident communication with engineers, customer technical teams, compliance officers and executives, in fluent written and spoken English.


Nice to Have

  • Telecom experience, for example mobile voice and SMS, MVNO platforms, SIP, call recording or CDRs.
  • Compliance or regtech experience, such as communications recording, archiving or surveillance.
  • Experience shipping AI features in production, such as speech-to-text, LLM evaluation or human-in-the-loop review.

Benefits

Why 1GLOBAL?

  • Growth Opportunities: Advance your career in one of the fastest growing telecommunications companies, expanding over 50% year-on-year under the leadership of successful tech entrepreneurs.
  • Major Transaction Exposure: Be in the driver’s seat for transactions that will have an impact on the future telco industry.
  • Work with a Talented Team: From the Board and the Founders to the Senior Management Team, you will collaborate daily with the most capable and renowned external advisors and constantly being exposed to talented and driven individuals.
  • Dynamic Work Environment: Thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced workplace where innovation is encouraged, and every contribution counts.
  • Professional Development: Work alongside industry experts to enhance your skills and knowledge in a cutting-edge field.
  • International Experience: Gain opportunities to work in different 1GLOBAL offices around the world as you grow within the company.
  • Open Communication Culture: Join a team where your ideas are heard, and open dialogue is encouraged, fostering a supportive and transparent work environment.
  • Get Things Done Attitude: Be part of a results-driven team that values efficiency, creativity, and the drive to make a tangible impact in the industry.


1GLOBAL is an equal opportunity employer, we value your character as much as your talent. Diversity drives our innovation, and we offer a collaborative, dynamic, and international work environment. We are excited for you to join our mission to revolutionise connectivity globally.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description:
About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The role

You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.

Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.

We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

What you'll do

  • Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
  • Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.
  • Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.
  • Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
  • Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
  • Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

  • You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
  • You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
  • You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
  • You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
  • You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
  • You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we'd like to speak to you.

We'd be thrilled if you had

  • Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.

title: Communications Lead

About Peec AI

AI search is changing how brands are discovered and chosen. People now ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Google’s AI answers what they used to search for, and AI assistants increasingly shape the journey from discovery to purchase. Winning customers now means winning over the AI systems that influence their decisions.

Peec AI is an AI search platform that helps marketing teams understand and improve how their brands are discovered, represented, and recommended. We’re a Series A company backed by 20VC and Singular, with 100+ people across our Berlin HQ and our New York office.

About the role

We publish a lot of original evidence about AI search: a quarterly industry report, a public Index, and findings from our own research team. Right now each piece reaches the market on its own, and nobody owns the story that connects them.

We're hiring a Communications Lead to own that story. You'll decide the few ideas Peec should be known for, write and edit the work that carries them, and keep them consistent across research, founder comms, press, events, social and campaigns.

This is a senior individual contributor role based in Berlin. You report to the VP of Growth and work directly with our founders, our product marketer, and our research and content team.

What you'll do

  • Decide what Peec is known for. Pick the two or three ideas we want to own, the evidence behind each, and how the story develops quarter to quarter. Write it down so the rest of the company can repeat it.

  • Turn research into stories. Work with the research team to find what in the data our audience will care about most, then carry it out: the report intro, the founder post, the journalist brief, the stage premise. Same evidence, told differently for each audience.

  • Shape our social strategy. You set what Peec and our founders talk about on social and how each story runs across LinkedIn and our other channels. The social and content team runs the channels day to day. Work with product marketing so launches and the brand story say the same thing.

  • Write and edit the highest-stakes work yourself. Founder and expert pieces, press materials, campaign copy and research comms. Brief writers and producers on the rest, and hold every contributor to the same bar.

  • Run founder and expert communications. Talking points, interview prep, opinion pieces, stage remarks and founder posts on LinkedIn, with honest feedback afterwards. Make our founders and experts consistently good on the record.

  • Lead press and publisher strategy. Bring the news judgment, angles and briefing materials, and pitch journalists yourself. Treat independent coverage and sponsored placements differently.

  • Make Peec citable in AI search. We help marketing teams see and improve how AI search talks about them. Our own story should be the best-cited example in the category, and you own how ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini describe Peec.

What we're looking for

  • You've led an integrated launch at a B2B tech company, taking original research or a complex product to a clear story shipped across channels. You can walk us from raw evidence to final assets: what you wrote, what you commissioned, where the story changed and what you refused to claim.

  • You write fast, in many formats, and in someone else's voice when needed. We'll ask for recent work where your part is clear.

  • You are comfortable with data. Given a set of metrics, you can say which story holds up to a sceptical reader and which one doesn't.

  • You've pitched journalists yourself and landed coverage.

  • You've built the function rather than only contributed. Early or growth stage, first or second in seat.

  • You build your own tools. AI is part of how you draft, monitor and research, and you can show us your setup and where you stop letting it write for you.

  • You work directly with founders, make decisions and ship.

Bonus points

title: Director of Procurement & Trading
description:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

title: UI Engineer (Based in CA or NC only)
description:
Mission: Live at the intersection of app runtime & security. Protect applications in a fundamental way so that developers can build great application services and not be constantly looking over their shoulder. BlueRock is changing the landscape of App runtime security.

The role

Location: Must be based in CA (preferably San Francisco Bay Area) or North Carolina

You will work alongside BlueRock's product designers and the control plane development team on our operator consoles. These are the React front ends that engineers and security teams use to manage large fleets of protected nodes, see what AI agents are actually doing across those fleets, and author the policy that constrains them.

The domain is AI and agentic systems, seen from the operations and security side. When an agent calls an MCP server, spawns a subagent, runs a shell command in a sandbox, or burns $40 of tokens in an afternoon, our UI is where a person sees it, understands it, and decides what to allow. So the interesting problems are visibility problems (how do you show a thousand agent sessions so someone can find the one that matters?) and control problems (how do you author an enforcement policy without a mistake taking production down?).

This is a mid-level role. We expect about 3–5 years of professional front-end experience, or equivalent work that clearly shows the same judgment. The ideal candidate is passionate about user experience, design, and AI-assisted software development, with a demonstrated grounding in engineering best practices. The title says UI, but the work doesn’t stop there: you’ll work closely with our backend services, and a feature is finished when it’s proven working live, not when the screen looks right.

Working with design delivered as code

At BlueRock, product designers design and collaborate in code. Instead of handing off static mockups, they build working UI with AI coding tools, against real data, and open merge requests. Iteration happens so quickly that it has outpaced our capacity for robust engineering collaboration and review.

This role closes that gap. You will collaborate directly with product designers and backend developers to keep UI development fast, by bridging the gap between vibe code and high-quality, sustainable, well-tested code. Some days that means reviewing and hardening a designer's branch so it can merge. Other days it means building the shared components, tests and guardrails that make the next branch need less hardening.

Beyond reviewing and hardening code, you'll help shape how it gets made. Working with designers and the AI tools they use, you'll turn what each review teaches us into shared components, conventions, tests and agent instructions. Over time the whole practice becomes more predictable, and each new branch arrives closer to production-ready.

Roles and collaboration

Software development roles are blurring more than ever. This role reports to product design, with API and data-layer guidance from our control plane engineering lead. You must be attuned to the perspectives of both UX/Design and Engineering, acting as a bridge between the goals and priorities of both sides, while ultimately deferring to UX/design partners on matters of style, copy, and information architecture.

In practice: when a designer's branch makes a choice about layout, copy or flow, you protect the intent and fix the implementation. When the implementation can't support the intent, because of performance, data shape or maintainability, you say so early and bring options rather than quietly changing the design.

What you'll do

  • Review designer-authored merge requests and bring them to production quality: structure, types, tests, accessibility, performance, and both light and dark themes.

  • Turn one-off UI from fast iteration into shared, documented components in our design system and Storybook, and migrate the apps onto them.

  • Make data-dense views hold up at real scale. Dashboards, tables, charts, and time-range and filter controls that work on a demo tenant also have to work on one with billions of events.

  • Wire UI to the API layer (GraphQL), and work with backend developers when a view needs a new query, field or endpoint.

  • Own UI test coverage: Vitest for units and Playwright for end-to-end flows, kept green in CI.

  • Test UI end to end in live, secured environments, with full authentication and authorization, real data and realistic load, before calling it done.

  • Keep UI work moving across release lines: shipping behind feature flags, and carrying fixes between branches when a release is frozen.

  • Fix UI bugs across the consoles and the Windows, Mac and Linux clients: layout and overflow, tooltips and popovers, empty and zero states, things that are technically correct and still confusing.

  • When needed, design new interfaces within the existing design system, and bring them to design for review.

  • Help set the guardrails that make AI-assisted UI development safe: lint rules, conventions, review checklists, and the instructions our AI coding tools follow.

How we expect you to work

These are the habits of a careful engineer. They matter more here, not less, because so much of the code you touch was drafted quickly by someone else or by an AI tool.

  1. Diagnose before you change. Find the actual cause, which is usually a layer away from the symptom, and be able to explain why your fix addresses it. A change that makes the symptom disappear is not the same as a fix.

  2. Small, deliberate diffs. Solve the problem in front of you. Don't refactor adjacent code on the way past, and don't build the abstraction you may need later.

  3. Fix it in one place. When the same bug shows up in three panels, the fix belongs in the shared component, not copied three times. Knowing where a change belongs is most of the skill.

  4. Verify, then claim. Run it, look at it, check both themes and a narrow viewport, get types and lint clean, and write the test where a test is what proves it. Then say plainly what you checked and what you did not. This applies double to AI-assisted work: you own the diff, whoever drafted it.

  5. Say when you're unsure. A requirement with two readings is a question, not a guess. Surfacing a problem early is always cheaper than discovering it in review.

Our UI stack and design system

Our front ends are several React and TypeScript apps that share one codebase: our enterprise operator consoles and our cloud product for builders.

All of them are built on our own design system. It is a shared React component library on top of Ant Design, with design tokens for color, type and spacing, light and dark themes, and a shared app shell for navigation, page layout and headers. Every component is documented in Storybook, published from CI, which serves as the reference for designers, engineers and AI coding tools alike. The library also carries written instructions for AI coding assistants, so generated code reaches for the system's components and tokens instead of inventing its own.

A large part of this role is the design system itself. That means promoting patterns out of individual apps into shared components, writing their stories, keeping tokens and themes consistent so the apps don't drift, and making the system the easiest path for anyone, or any agent, building UI.

  • Front end: React, TypeScript, Vite

  • Design system: our component library built on Ant Design, including design tokens and light and dark themes

  • Documentation: Storybook, published to GitLab Pages

  • Data and charts: GraphQL; ECharts for the data-dense views

  • Testing: Vitest, Playwright, and contract and smoke suites in CI

  • Delivery: GitLab merge requests and pipelines, release branches, feature flags

  • Further back: TypeScript and Rust services over graph and columnar stores, built on OpenTelemetry, plus desktop apps and services across Mac, Windows and Linux

You don't need experience with all of it. You do need to be strong in TypeScript and React, and willing to read code before changing it.

What you bring

  • About 3–5 years building production front ends in TypeScript and modern React: hooks, composition, state that lives at the right level, and an understanding of why a re-render happens.

  • An end-to-end view of the systems behind the UI. Designing in code gets a feature most of the way to working, and you close the rest of the gap. For you, “done” doesn’t stop at the UI working. It means the UI is integrated and shown to work live, in a secured environment with full authentication and authorization, under realistic load.

  • Integration testing against complex backends. Tests that only run against mock data in a standalone dev stack aren’t enough here. You can create, integrate and run tests in live environments to check data validity, load, security and scale, and you keep unit, integration and end-to-end suites green in CI.

  • Performance instincts for data-heavy UI: pagination, virtualization, server-side filtering, and knowing when a slow page is a query problem rather than a rendering problem.

  • A track record of reviewing other people’s code and improving it without rewriting it.

  • Git in complex repositories with several active release branches, where a single fix may need to be cherry-picked, ported or graft-merged onto more than one of them. Readable commits, and responding to review without taking it personally.

  • Hands-on use of AI coding tools in real work, with clear habits for checking what they produce.

  • CSS that holds up: flexbox and grid, overflow and scroll containers, responsive behaviour, and why a tooltip or popover ends up clipped.

  • Experience building or contributing to a component library or design system, ideally with Storybook and design tokens.

  • Careful attention to visual detail and real interest in UX. Much of this work is noticing that something is two pixels wrong, or that a label is technically correct and still confusing.

  • Genuine interest in the AI and agentic space, and in the operational and security questions it creates.

Nice to have: Ant Design; GraphQL; ECharts or other charting libraries; design training or a portfolio; experience on a team where designers commit code; writing conventions or instructions for AI coding tools; desktop UI across Mac, Windows and Linux; dense operational tooling such as observability, security or infrastructure products.

Not required: a computer science degree, if your work shows the same rigor. Deep backend, security or infrastructure expertise, or any knowledge of our domain (fleet management, telemetry, agent observability, policy enforcement). We will teach that.

Your first 90 days

  1. First month: land changes safely. Ship scoped fixes in the consoles. Learn the component library, theme tokens and API layer. Start reviewing designer merge requests alongside an engineer.

  2. Second month: own review on a surface. Become the primary reviewer for designer-authored UI on one product area, and extract at least one repeated pattern into a shared component.

  3. Third month: make the next branch easier. Get the flows you own covered by tests in CI, and write down the conventions and guardrails that make designer branches need less hardening.

BlueRock changes the game, enabling organizations to shift from chasing CVEs and exploits to proactively protecting the foundations of applications and computing, so that developers can build great applications without looking over their shoulders.

Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.

About the Role

We're looking for a natural Sales person who is passionate about hospitality. Sales is at the heart of our business growth right now, and you will be driving it forward in your day-to-day. This role is about more than closing deals, it is about blending with the hospitality scene and winning the market.

In your day-to-day you can expect a mix of top of funnel activities, field sales, cold sales, networking, events and more.

What You’ll Do

Our sales are not your typical SaaS or office sales. We meet our customers where they operate:

  • Find the coolest new hospitality spots in town that everyone talks about

  • Create engaging ways to show our product

  • Use creative communication strategies to close the deal that will help the merchant operate smarter

  • Do a smooth handover to the onboarding team to make sure we go live quickly and successfully

  • Efficiently use our CRM and other Sales tools (Hubspot, Clay, AI) to leave more time for creativity and connection

  • Continuously improve and revisit our sales funnel

  • Keep an eye on the new developments in the industry and the merchants needs to create our own path

What You’ll Need

You are a natural relationship builder with a passion for hospitality industry:

  • Hands-on approach, independence and hunger for fast-paced operations

  • Natural curiosity and a healthy appetite for calculated risk - we want you to try new things and not be afraid to fail

  • Strong and engaging communication skills - you can grab an attention of a busy hospitality owner and keep them interested

  • Passion and curiosity for hospitality and hospitality tech

  • Competitive Salary

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

title: Montu Pharmacy Assessment Centre
description:
Ready to start or take the next step in your pharmacy career?

At Montu, we are doing things differently, and that includes how we recruit.

We are growing, and we are looking for enthusiastic, hardworking and patient-focused individuals to join our pharmacy team in Winnersh Triangle.

Whether you are looking to take your first step into healthcare, explore a new career in pharmacy or bring your existing pharmacy experience to a rapidly growing organisation, we would love to meet you.

We are hosting a Pharmacy Assessment Centre on Wednesday 18th November, giving you the opportunity to experience a different approach to recruitment, demonstrate your skills and learn more about what it is like to work at Montu.

You do not need previous pharmacy experience for all of our opportunities. For our entry-level positions, what matters most is your attitude, willingness to learn and genuine commitment to making a difference to patients.

Our pharmacy is busy. Really busy. It is a lively, energetic environment where things move quickly, teamwork is essential and no two days are quite the same. If you enjoy being on your feet, working alongside others and being part of a team where everyone has a role to play, you could feel right at home.

Behind every prescription we process is a patient relying on us to get things right. Whether you are packing medication, dispensing prescriptions or completing final accuracy checks, your contribution matters.

Opportunities Available

We are recruiting across several positions within our pharmacy team, with opportunities for both experienced pharmacy professionals and individuals looking to enter the industry.

Pharmacy Assistant

An excellent entry point into the pharmacy sector, with no previous pharmacy experience required.

You will support the day-to-day operations of our busy pharmacy, including preparing orders, packing medication, supporting stock management and helping ensure prescriptions are processed accurately and efficiently.

We are looking for individuals who are organised, reliable, comfortable with repetitive tasks and enjoy working in a hands-on, fast-paced environment.

Trainee Pharmacy Dispenser

Looking to develop a career in pharmacy? This could be your opportunity.

No previous dispensing experience is required. You will receive training and support as you develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to work within our dispensing team.

You will learn about prescription processing, medication handling, accuracy, pharmacy procedures and the importance of maintaining high standards of patient safety.

Pharmacy Dispenser

For individuals with an existing dispensing qualification and experience working within a pharmacy environment.

You will support the safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, working closely with pharmacists, technicians and the wider pharmacy team.

You will need excellent attention to detail, a strong understanding of pharmacy procedures and the ability to maintain accuracy while managing high prescription volumes.

Accuracy Checking Dispenser

We are looking for qualified and experienced Accuracy Checking Dispensers who can help maintain the high standards of accuracy and patient safety expected within our pharmacy.

You will undertake accuracy checking duties within the scope of your qualification, training and authorisation, supporting the efficient processing of prescriptions and working collaboratively with the wider team.

Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT)

For qualified Pharmacy Technicians with an accredited accuracy checking qualification and current GPhC registration.

You will play an important role in maintaining dispensing accuracy, supporting pharmacy operations and ensuring our processes meet the required professional and regulatory standards.

You will bring confidence, attention to detail and the ability to work effectively in a high-volume dispensing environment.

What Is Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre?

We know that traditional interviews do not always give people the best opportunity to demonstrate what they can do.

That is why we are taking a slightly different approach.

Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre is designed to be an engaging, practical and interactive experience where you can demonstrate your abilities, meet members of the Montu team and gain a better understanding of our working environment.

You can expect a combination of practical and team-based activities designed to assess skills relevant to working within our pharmacy, including:

  • Attention to detail and accuracy

  • Literacy and the ability to follow written instructions

  • Working effectively with others

  • Organisation and the ability to follow processes

  • Speed and efficiency without compromising accuracy

  • Communication and problem-solving

We are not expecting everyone to arrive with pharmacy knowledge, particularly those applying for our entry-level opportunities.

We are interested in how you approach tasks, how you work with others and whether you have the right attitude to succeed in our environment.

What happens after the assessment centre?

Candidates who successfully complete the assessment centre will be invited to attend a further on-site interview at Montu on a later date.

Please note that attendance at the assessment centre does not guarantee an interview or offer of employment.

What Are We Looking For?

We are looking for people who genuinely want to be part of a team making a difference.

Our ideal candidates will be:

  • Patient-focused: You understand that the work you do has a direct impact on the people relying on our service.

  • Detail-oriented: Accuracy matters, particularly when working with medication.

  • Comfortable in a busy environment: You enjoy an energetic workplace and can remain focused when things get hectic.

  • Reliable and hardworking: You take pride in doing your job well and supporting the people around you.

  • Team players: You understand that pharmacy operations depend on people working together.

  • Adaptable: You are comfortable learning new processes and responding to change.

  • Eager to learn: Whether you are new to pharmacy or already experienced, you are motivated to develop your skills.

You do not need to be the loudest person in the room or have years of experience to succeed here.

What matters is your work ethic, your attention to detail and your commitment to doing things properly.

About Montu

Montu is a leading medical cannabis company working to improve access to cannabis-based medicines for patients across the UK.

Through our specialist clinical services and pharmacy operations, we support patients receiving prescribed cannabis-based medicines for a range of eligible medical conditions.

Our multidisciplinary teams bring together clinicians, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, dispensers and operational colleagues, all working towards the same goal: delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

We are a rapidly growing organisation, and our pharmacy is at the heart of what we do.

Every prescription represents a patient who is depending on us. From the moment a prescription reaches our pharmacy to the moment medication is dispatched, every member of our team plays an important role in that patient journey.

We are proud to be helping shape an evolving area of healthcare, and we want people who are excited to be part of that journey.

Why Join Montu?

Joining Montu means becoming part of a growing organisation where your work has purpose and your contribution makes a difference.

We offer:

  • Competitive salaries dependent on the position, qualifications and experience

  • Opportunities for training and professional development

  • Career progression within our growing pharmacy operations

  • A supportive and collaborative team environment

  • The opportunity to gain experience within a specialist area of healthcare

  • The chance to be part of a growing business helping improve patient access to prescribed medication

Further information about the benefits applicable to each role will be provided during the recruitment process.

Ready to Join Us?

description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Why this role exists

 

We are about to hire the people who will define the next phase of this company. Not backfill a plan someone else wrote — define it. The quality of who joins Dust over the next eighteen months is the single highest-leverage variable in whether we build the category or watch someone else do it.

 

That work needs a recruiter who treats hiring as a craft rather than a queue. Someone who can hold a real point of view on what "great" looks like for a role, defend it with a hiring manager who disagrees, and then go find that person themselves — from a cold start, without a lead gen team, a sourcing pod, or a playbook waiting for them.

 

You'll be an early member of a small Talent team. That means you own roles end to end, and you also help build the thing itself: the assessment design, the interview loops, the calibration, the data we use to know whether any of it is working.

 

We're looking for someone who cares about the candidate experience for all parties internal and external. And prioritizes protecting Dust's culture by being thoughtful, thorough and leading by example in being a true team player.

 
 

What you'll own

 

Full-cycle hiring, end to end. You run your own searches from role kickoff to close. Sourcing, outreach, screening, interviewing, offer strategy, negotiation. You are the owner of the outcome, not a coordinator of other people's opinions.

 

Assessment design, not just assessment delivery. For every role you open, you help define what evidence would actually predict success — then you build the loop that surfaces it. You'll push back on interview stages that exist out of habit and replace them with ones that test something real.

 

Hiring manager partnership with a spine. You'll spend as much time calibrating hiring managers as you do talking to candidates. When a manager says "not quite the right feel," you'll ask what they mean until there's a defensible answer, and you'll say so when there isn't one.

 

Market intelligence. You'll know your talent market better than anyone else in the building — who's good, where they are, what moves them, what compensation actually looks like right now — and you'll bring that back into how we scope roles and design offers.

 

The candidate experience. Our hiring process is the first honest sample of what working here feels like. You'll make it expedient, direct, well-communicated, and worth a candidate's time whether or not they get an offer.

 

Building the function. Process, tooling, structured scorecards, funnel data, quality-of-hire signal. You'll leave the system better than you found it, and you'll be trusted to change it without asking permission first.

 
 

Two tracks — tell us which one is yours

 

We're hiring for depth in one of two areas. You should have a genuine centre of gravity in one; interest in the other is a bonus, not a requirement.

 

GTM. Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Marketing, and the leaders above them, across Europe and the US. You know how to assess commercial talent on evidence rather than swagger, and you can tell the difference between a rep who carried a territory and a rep who inherited one.

 

Technical. Software engineers, infrastructure, product, and design, in a market where the best people are not looking and the second-best are drowning in outreach. You can hold a credible conversation about what someone actually built, and you know why that matters more than where they built it.

 
 

How we think about hiring

 

We're telling you this up front because if you disagree with it, this will be a frustrating job.

 

  • We don't hire based on pedigree. Logos and school names are weak evidence. What someone has actually done, and what they can demonstrate now, is strong evidence. We design our loops accordingly.

  • We hire for evidence, not affinity. "Culture fit" that means "reminds me of me" is how companies get homogeneous and slow. We assess against explicit behaviours tied to how we work, and we write down what we saw.

  • Speed and rigour are not in tension. Slow processes are usually a symptom of unclear thinking about the role, not of high standards.

  • A no should be as clear as a yes. To the candidate, and internally.

  • Some of us came from well-known companies. That's context, not criteria. It isn't why we're here and it won't be why you are. We celebrate everyone's achievements and want to create an environment where diversity of thought and experience of a collective whole makes this place exceptional and lasting.

  • Recruiters are operators, not order-takers. If you think a role is wrongly scoped, badly levelled, or shouldn't be open at all, you're expected to say so.

 
 

What we're looking for

 

  • 5+ years in full-cycle recruiting, with meaningful time in-house at a high-growth company. You've hired in an environment with real ambiguity, not just real volume.

  • Demonstrable depth in either GTM or technical hiring — you can talk through searches you've run, what made them hard, and what you'd do differently.

  • Genuinely strong sourcing. Not "I partner with a sourcing team." You find people yourself, and you write outreach that people reply to because it's obviously written by a human who read something.

  • Comfort operating without infrastructure. No playbook, no SDR equivalent, limited tooling to start.

  • The judgement and directness to challenge senior stakeholders, and the credibility to be listened to when you do.

  • A bias to start. You see the gap and close it before anyone asks you to.

  • Excellent written English and a real feel for language. Everything you write is a piece of our employer brand.

  • Low ego, high ownership. No job is too big or too small — you'll design an assessment framework in the morning and chase a scheduling conflict in the afternoon.

  • Based in Paris, London or New York.

 

Ideal, but not required: experience hiring in AI or developer-facing companies; experience building or improving a hiring process rather than inheriting one; multi-market hiring across Europe and the US.

 
 

You'll be using AI to do this job — properly

 

We build the AI operating system that companies use to rewire their work. We expect our own team to be the sharpest possible example of that.

 

You'll build and run your own Dust agents: market maps, candidate research, interview debrief synthesis, competitive intelligence on where talent is moving. Not as a side project — as how the job gets done. You don't need to have done this before, but you do need to be the kind of person who is genuinely excited to, rather than politely tolerant of it.

 

You'll also be one of our most credible internal sources of feedback on the product, because you'll be a heavy user of it every day.

 
 

Location

 

This role is based in Paris, London or New York, and we'd love you to spend real time in the office with the team. A lot of the best things about building at Dust happen because people are in the same room: the energy, the fast decisions, the unexpected conversation that unlocks a hard problem.

 

We hire people with strong judgement and extend that trust to how they manage their time.

 
 

Our process

 

We'll tell you the full loop up front, keep it to a small number of stages, and give you a decision quickly. You'll meet the people you'd work with, not a panel of proxies. Expect at least one stage where you work through a real hiring problem with us rather than describing a past one.

 

If you don't check every box, apply anyway. We're more interested in your potential and how you think than a perfect match to a checklist.

 

Please send your application and resume in English.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

description:
Health can’t wait.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Marketing Ops is one of Alan's highest-leverage functions.

It sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, data, and technology — turning systems into growth engines and ensuring every touchpoint with prospects and members is timely, relevant, and scalable.

Alan is growing fast across France, Belgium, Spain, and Canada. But today we're leaving value on the table. On the prospect side, we drive more traffic but can't convert it properly: no scoring, no intelligent routing, no nurturing that adapts to buying intent. On the member side, messaging is one of our primary touchpoints for engagement, retention, and trust — yet nobody operates it strategically. Personalization stays shallow, communication pressure goes unmonitored, and shipping a message often means filing an engineering ticket.

We need Marketing Ops leaders who can architect scalable systems, operate them strategically, and progressively embed AI into workflows — to raise quality, reduce manual execution, and unlock growth without scaling headcount linearly.

⭐️ The Marketing Ops job ⭐️

We are hiring two Marketing Operations Managers, each embedded in a different crew:

  • Growth Infrastructure — focused on prospect acquisition: building a unified lead engine that captures, scores, routes, and nurtures across all channels

  • Product Platform — focused on member lifecycle messaging: operating Alan's messaging stack as a scalable service across 1.7M+ profiles

Both roles share the same DNA: strong marketing ops fundamentals, data fluency, a product mindset, and the ability to be both hands-on and strategic. Crew placement will be determined based on the candidate's experience, interests, and fit during the hiring process.

Why is this role interesting?

  • Speed: marketing, product, and sales teams ship campaigns and messages confidently — Marketing Ops turns bottlenecks into force multipliers across every crew

  • Trust: clean data, governed attributes, proper segmentation, and enforced rules mean the right person gets the right message at the right time

  • Scale: as we grow to millions of members across multiple countries, we need operators who keep our platforms clean and the user experience protected — without scaling headcount linearly

  • AI at the frontier: this isn't a maintenance role — you'll identify high-priority use cases for AI agents, train and refine them to a senior marketer's quality bar, and drive real adoption

What will you do with us?

You'll be a partnership with marketers — not a service desk. You'll partner closely with engineers, data, designers, and cross-functional stakeholders (PMMs, sales, growth, product) within a PM-Tech duo crew model.

Regardless of crew, you will own a core set of capabilities:

  • Marketing Automation & CRM: own and optimize our marketing stack (Customer.io, CRM integrations); build automations that enable marketers to launch campaigns independently, at scale, across all geos

  • Data Model & Governance: maintain CRM data quality, attribute/event design, and database hygiene as a sustained practice

  • Segmentation & Lifecycle Design: design and maintain lifecycle stages, segmentation logic, routing rules, and re-engagement flows across multiple audiences and geos

  • Nurturing Infrastructure: own the nurturing stack and campaign processes; make launches autonomous and compliant

  • AI-First Operations: identify, build, and refine AI agents for email copywriting, lead scoring, next-best-action recommendations, and content generation — making marketers AI-powered, not replacing them

  • Performance Monitoring: track the full funnel from first touchpoint to conversion; identify leakage and prioritize from data

  • Documentation & Enablement: create playbooks, train teams on tools and processes, reduce the marginal cost of new campaigns

Then, depending on your crew:

Growth Infrastructure — you'll build a unified lead engine (no more tool-by-tool silos), design lead scoring and routing models, crack multi-channel activation (email, WhatsApp, Voice AI), build AI agents that pre-qualify and enrich leads, and maintain a live feedback loop with BDRs, AEs, and Inbound Sales.

Product Platform — you'll operate Customer.io and back-end triggered emails as one governed system, monitor communication pressure and enforce channel rules, define and enforce recipient lifecycle paths, drive 100% Design Studio adoption, and co-own outbound messaging strategy with PMMs and product teams.

By your first year, we'll know it worked when:

  • At least one AI agent is in production on a key use case (email nurturing, lead categorization, content generation), with a second scoped or live, and adoption is real

  • Any marketer or product Alaner can launch a campaign or ship a message without bottlenecking through ops or engineering

  • CRM data model, attributes, and segments are properly owned, documented, and clean — the data we see is data we can act on

  • Every contact has a documented path through our messaging — segmentation is sharp, messaging is relevant, and pressure is monitored

  • Marketing's contribution to acquisition and engagement is visible and quantifiable, from first touch to conversion


⭐️ Is it you we are looking for? ⭐️


You'll be a great fit for this opportunity if you:

  • Have 5+ years in Marketing operations, growth ops, CRM ops, lifecycle marketing, or lead generation in a tech environment (B2B, B2C, or B2B2C)

  • Have hands-on experience managing marketing automation platforms at scale (Customer.io, Braze, Iterable, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, Salesforce, or equivalent)

  • Have a strong understanding of CRM data models — attribute/event design and data hygiene as a sustained practice

  • Can frame and implement processes for lead scoring, nurturing, segmentation, and personalization

  • Have a product knack: you can define what's not working, identify what to build next, and see problems as opportunities to bring more value

  • Bring data fluency and analytical rigor: you read platform and campaign data, surface anomalies, and draw business insights

  • Can be both hands-on and think strategically — you drive the big picture while staying close to execution

  • Have strong stakeholder management skills — you'll partner daily with engineering, product, sales, and marketing teams

  • Can manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-moving environment

  • Communicate with excellent written and spoken English

  • Are impact-driven with a strong bias towards improving processes

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range.

🙌 Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer:

  • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary, for permanent contracts only.

  • Flexible office with hybrid setup. Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or sponsored co-working hubs in Bordeaux, Lyon, Marseille, Nantes, Biarritz, Annecy, Brussels, Madrid or Barcelona.

Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description:
What Quadrants is

Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.

The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.

It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.

The role

You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.

Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.

Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.

What you’ll own

  • IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.

  • Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.

  • Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.

  • Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works.

  • The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction.

Who you are

You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward.

The ground that judgment stands on:

  • GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus.

People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder.

How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound.

Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.

This is at the core of Genesis AI's strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Research applied end-to-end, from algorithm to merged, tested, documented code that real robot-learning pipelines depend on. Occasional groundbreaking research happens, notably through academic collaborations. But the core of the job is making the engine measurably better along five axes:

  • Speed. Algorithms that are not only faster but also smart enough to spend compute only where it matters across both time and space: larger stable timesteps, selective fidelity (adaptive across scales or simply hand-set), structure-aware solvers.

  • Completeness. No physics off limits: water, human animation, air flow, gravel, tendons, even body organs. Whatever the next use-case needs, the engine grows to cover it.

  • Fidelity. More realistic models: contact, friction, deformation, energy, actuation, materials…

  • Versatility. Extensible multi-physics without compromise on realism: all solvers in the scene coupled together at once, two-way and constraint-based. Write your own solver and it joins the scene like a native one, growing into an open solver ecosystem.

  • Scalability. From workstation to factory scale, and one day, city scale: thousands of interacting entities, batched across environments, without losing physical soundness.

Our ambition is to establish Genesis-World as the go-to simulator for physical AI, from companies and research labs to individuals.

  • Every fidelity for every physics. The same physics at every point of the speed-accuracy spectrum, from heavily batched training with XPBD or VBD to final validation with IPC. Same scene, same API, pick your tradeoff.

  • Invent physics level-of-detail (LOD). Rendering has had LOD for decades, physics is still waiting. Simulate at full fidelity what agents interact with and see, coarsely what they do not.

  • Heterogeneous environments. Every parallel world can hold a completely different model: different bodies, joints, and collision geometries.

  • Adaptive timesteps per island. Error-based control with Runge-Kutta Dopri5, and Time-of-Impact stepping during collision detection, as done in Jiminy.

  • Closed kinematic loops without constraints. Handle loops intrinsically for numerical stability and speed, in the spirit of Kamino.

Day to day: you write your physics in plain Python and Quadrants makes it fast on every backend. And you validate it the hard way: analytical closed forms, other engines, real-world data.

Who you are

You are a physicist and an engineer at once. You judge a method by whether it holds up in production at real scale, and you do not stop until it does. No blind spots: you relentlessly hunt down even the defect that looks insignificant, because it never is.
