Staff Platform Engineer, Agentic Engineering

Developer Productivity · AI Coding Agents · Developer Platform

Our ambition: an engineering organisation where humans and agents work as one continuously learning system, turning frontier AI capabilities and real-world feedback into more ambitious product development. We want n8n to be the reference for how this is done, without compromising quality, resilience or trust. Your main goal is to make that real.

This is a Staff individual contributor role in Developer Platform and the technical driving force behind ACDC (Agent-centric Development Cycle), our engineering-wide initiative for agentic development. Nobody has a playbook for this yet. You'll write ours.

You won't start from zero. Agents wired into Linear already automate around 80% of the development cycle on one of our developer platform projects, alongside pilots for insight, feature-flag and PR-review agents and a shared agent harness. Your job is to take this from promising experiments to the way n8n builds software.

This role is for someone who thinks about this problem constantly. You run agents all day, rebuild your own workflow every time the frontier moves, and have more ideas than time.

You'll stay hands-on, building the first versions yourself, and shape how the work grows beyond one person.

What you'll do

Set direction and own the outcome

  • Identify where agentic development can make the greatest difference, using developer feedback, existing experiments and engineering performance data.

  • Set the strategy and priorities across agent execution, repository readiness, CI, security and developer workflows.

  • Make build, buy or pass decisions on tools and vendors, and own the cost and value trade-offs, including AI spend.

  • Make decisions where requirements are incomplete and the trade-offs between autonomy, reliability, security and review effort are still emerging.

  • Build alignment through technical proposals, clear decisions and working software, and report progress and impact to engineering leadership.

Build the foundations

  • Design and build isolated execution environments where agents can work with the right access to code, tools and context, without exposing secrets or sensitive systems.

  • Own the safety model: which task categories agents may attempt, what they must never touch, and where human review is required, partnering with Security on sensitive areas like auth, billing, permissions and data handling.

  • Make n8n's monorepo agent-ready, working with Architecture and senior engineers on repo structure, testability, boundaries and the context agents need.

Integrate agents into how we work

  • Build repeatable workflows that take Linear issues through agent execution, self-verification and review to merged PRs, across a growing range of task types.

  • Integrate agentic workflows with GitHub, CI, test infrastructure and code review, so the agentic path becomes the easiest path for engineers.

  • Extend the loop beyond coding: connect earlier signals like product research and customer requests, and later ones like production metrics, so agents contribute across the whole cycle.

  • Open it up beyond engineering, so PMs, designers and others can turn a well-defined issue into a reviewed, mergeable change.

  • Shape review practices, such as PR evidence that shows what changed, what ran, what risks remain and where human judgment is needed.

Measure what works

  • Build benchmarks from real historical engineering tasks to evaluate output quality, failure modes, review burden and production risk.

  • Define and track quality and adoption signals, such as reviewer acceptance rate, CI pass rate, rework rate and developer satisfaction.

  • Use data and feedback to change course, retire what doesn't work, and build trust across engineering.

Must-haves

  • 🧭 Staff-scope ownership: You’ve led complex platform, DevEx or engineering productivity initiatives across teams, from defining the problem to sustained adoption and measurable impact, where there was no established approach to follow.

  • 🤖 Agentic depth: You use coding agents daily as a power user, and you've built infrastructure around them, such as repo context and instructions, tool or MCP integrations, sandboxed execution or agent workflows in CI, that other engineers rely on.

  • 🎯 Product mindset for internal platforms: You treat engineers as your customers. You start from real friction, prioritise by impact, make build-vs-buy calls, weigh cost against value, and let adoption tell you whether something works.

  • 🤝 Direction without authority: You've set technical direction that multiple teams followed, through proposals, design reviews and credibility with senior engineers across Platform, Product Engineering, AI, Security and Architecture.

  • 🔐 Safety judgment: You've made real decisions on permissions, secrets, sandboxing, sensitive code paths and human-in-the-loop review, and can explain the trade-offs.

  • 📊 Measurement that drives decisions: You've built evaluations, benchmarks or quality metrics and used them to change course or retire things that didn't work. You care about outcomes, not lines of AI-generated code.

  • ✍️ Writing that changes decisions: Your technical proposals and documentation have shifted what teams did.

  • 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Growing a team: You've mentored engineers or helped shape a new team as an initiative grew beyond one person.

  • 🏢 B2B SaaS context: You understand environments where reliability, permissions, data handling and customer trust are central.

  • 🔗 Workflow automation: You're familiar with workflow automation, integration platforms, AI orchestration or developer-facing products.

You will also own the boundary between the vehicle and the backend: clear, versioned contracts with cloud services, deployment systems, video infrastructure, and operator interfaces that work over intermittent, low-bandwidth links.   • Design stable, versioned vehicle-to-backend contracts for telemetry, commands and acknowledgements, video metadata and control, configuration, health, and logs.

  • Engineer for unreliable connectivity: buffering and store-and-forward, idempotent commands, explicit acknowledgements and timeouts, reconnection, back-off, and safe behaviour when the backend is unreachable.

The Senior Data Business Analyst / Product Owner is a senior, client-facing member of the Data Products function who leads projects or individual domains within Data Transformation engagements, from the earliest Discovery and Scoping conversations through to Agile delivery and sign-off.

Alongside hands-on requirements, backlog and data analysis work, the Senior Consultant owns the Discovery and Design phase on their projects or domains within Data Transformation engagements, producing a clear scope baseline that enables Programme Management to run change control and enables Account Management to identify growth opportunities. The role brings a consulting mindset: structured problem framing, confident facilitation with senior business stakeholders, and a consistent focus on measurable client value.

  • Anticipated start date: January 2027

  • Location: EMEA - UK, Hungary, Bulgaria, Slovakia, Italy, Spain, Portugal

  • Daily rate: up to 420 GBP

  • Contract duration: 6 months

  • Project duration: December 2026 - June 2027

  • Daily Requirement: 8 hours per day, Monday to Friday

Key Responsibilities

Discovery & Design

  • Lead pre-project Discovery and Scoping for projects or individual domains within client Data Transformation engagements, applying Infinite Lambda's Discovery & Design framework, standards and artefacts

  • Define project objectives, preliminary requirements and scope boundaries with sufficient clarity to significantly de-risk the subsequent programme or project execution

  • Define data products end to end, including consumers, data contracts and ownership

  • Negotiate trade-offs on scope, timeline and resourcing with client stakeholders without escalating

Requirements Management

description:
About Aphex

We're the construction coordination platform that's replacing outdated spreadsheets with multiplayer tools that delivery teams love. Major contractors like BAM, Balfour Beatty, SKANSKA, Kier, MACE, and Murphy use Aphex to deliver their projects ranging from £50 million to multi-billion pound mega projects.

Since launching in 2019, we've grown to become the market-leading solution in the UK and Australia, with aspirations to be where every major project in the world is planned and delivered.

We're tackling an industry that drives 10% of global GDP yet has seen productivity decline for 20 years. It's time for change.

 

The Role

As a Customer Success Associate at Aphex, you'll learn our Land & Expand Engine inside one of the highest-paced teams at the company: the UK Customer Success Hub.

Your job is to help major contractors get genuine value out of Aphex on their live projects. You'll be in the room and on site with planners, engineers, construction managers, and project directors, helping them embed weekly planning routines, daily coordination, and the reporting that makes their projects run better.

This is a fast progression role. You'll start in apprentice mode alongside the UK CS team, learning the playbook by doing it. Within 6 to 9 months, most CSAs are running their own portfolio of projects as full Customer Success Managers. We hire people who are hungry for that progression and ready to earn it from day one, not waiting until month nine.

The team you're joining is in the middle of a step change: scaling the UK book and expanding into new geographical markets. The CSAs we hire now are part of how the UK CS function holds together and grows through that period.

AI is part of how the team works at Aphex. We expect everyone to use it to think, write, plan, and analyse better. Genuine curiosity about how AI can multiply your output is part of the job.

At Aphex we challenge the status quo as a default. As you grow in this role, you'll be expected to propose better ways of working and make them real, not wait for someone to ask.

 

What you'll learn and do

  • Run project deployments. Shadow experienced CSMs through kickoffs, setups, and training, then take the lead on your own.

  • Embed planning routines. Help major contractor teams establish the weekly planning cycle that becomes their project's operating rhythm.

  • Drive daily coordination. Move teams from weekly planning into the daily routines that make site coordination genuinely better.

  • Build trusted relationships across the project. Engineers, supervisors, planners, project managers, construction managers. Hold real credibility at every level.

  • Monitor project health and act on it. Track signals, spot risks early, run plays to fix issues before they escalate.

 

The team you'll join

You'll be part of the UK Customer Success Hub, working directly alongside four Customer Success Managers who collectively support projects worth billions in construction value across the UK's largest contractors. You'll learn by working live deployments with them, not from a training course.

You'll also work closely with our UK sales team to understand how project success translates into account growth, and collaborate with our APAC hub on shared accounts, knowledge sharing, and the global playbook we run across regions.

 

Why this matters

Every project you help succeed means a real project gets delivered better. Less waste, less delay, less rework, less pressure on the people doing the work. You're not just supporting software adoption, you're helping the UK's biggest contractors deliver the infrastructure and buildings the country actually needs.

 

About You

At Aphex, we believe our team should reflect the variety of perspectives in the world we build for. We've noticed that qualified candidates from underrepresented groups sometimes hesitate to apply unless they meet 100% of the listed requirements, while others might apply when meeting just 60%. If you're excited about Aphex and believe you have the core skills to succeed in this role, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't check every box. Your unique perspective might be exactly what we need.

  • You build trust quickly with people across all kinds of roles and seniority. You've held real relationships beyond the transaction. People you've worked with before still take your call.

  • You've been thrown in over your head and figured it out. At least one specific story (probably more) of taking on something you weren't qualified for and getting up to speed fast.

  • You don't wait to be asked. When you spot something that isn't working (a broken process, a missing resource, an awkward workflow), you take it on yourself to fix it.

The Mission: Why We Exist

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

A Day in the Life

At Genomics, we tackle major scientific challenges in harnessing genomic data to improve human health.

This role is part of the Life Sciences team, working on a range of challenges spanning the therapeutic development cycle – including discovering and validating therapeutic targets and developing patient stratification strategies. The Scientist is an early-career member of the team, who will thrive in a highly collaborative team environment. With the team’s support, you will develop and execute innovative and rigorous scientific approaches, and will effectively communicate findings to both internal and external stakeholders.

For example, a Scientist may:

  • Generate novel therapeutic hypothesis for diseases with unmet need, mining the in-house data resources using statistical approaches to understand the causal pathophysiology of disease, identify and triage potential targets with genetic evidence, and build a rich understanding of the cell types, cellular function, tissue-level characteristics, patient populations and biomarkers needed to support a development program.

  • Apply and optimise risk tools for patient stratification that combine genetic information (through polygenic risk scores) with conventional risk factors, to find those individuals most at risk of disease onset or progression and those most likely to benefit from particular therapies.

To be successful in this role, you will: bring a strong foundation in the application of statistical and computational techniques in biomedical science that you can apply in innovative ways, thrive on analysing vast and diverse sources of ‘omic data using leading statistical or AI/ML approaches to make meaningful insights into complex problems, and take pride in effectively sharing your findings with others.

Who You Are

Must have, solid foundations in:

  • Statistics (modelling, regression)

  • Genetics and molecular biology

  • Statistical programming (e.g., Python or R)

Preferred:

  • Experience using a broad array of statistical genetics approaches (e.g., GWAS, colocalization, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization, polygenic risk scores)

  • Experience defining phenotypes from electronic health records.

  • Knowledge of Bayesian inference, high dimensional statistics, causal inference.

  • Experience with software engineering practices (version control [Git & GitHub], testing, documentation, agentic coding, containerisation)

  • Experience building and running reproducible pipelines e.g., using WDL, Snakemake, or NextFlow.

  • Experience using cloud computing and trusted research environments e.g. DNAnexus or Verily Workbench.

  • Experience with methods development within statistical genetics

  • Clear Career Path: A straightforward, open progression framework means you'll always know the path to promotion and how to achieve your next career goal.

  • Financial & Health Security: Robust benefits including a market-leading pension scheme, comprehensive private health insurance for you and your family with NO excess, critical illness, and life assurance.

description:
Set a new pulse for healthcare!

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to join our team in Berlin.

Working in the tech team at Doctolib means building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead a team of 6 to 7 engineers of mixed seniority, owning delivery, quality and production health end to end — keeping engagement high and standards higher

  • Together with your product partner, define the mission and vision for your team and build a roadmap you can defend to stakeholders

  • Take part in architecture reviews and help shape the technical direction of the Scheduling stream, including the migration of core scheduling capabilities from the monolith into purpose-built services

  • Set and uphold the security, reliability, performance and scalability standards required to remain the most trusted e-health SaaS in Europe

  • Partner with Talent and People teams to recruit, develop and retain engineers through career conversations and feedback they can act on

  • Embed AI-assisted engineering into how your team works day to day, with a clear and honest view of where it helps and where it does not

  • Continuously improve how the team operates — planning, on-call, bug backlog, incident follow-up — so the team spends its energy on what moves the needle

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Have at least 6 years of software engineering experience and 3 years of engineering management experience, including leading a team of 5+ engineers through delivery, hiring and growth

  • Are credible with senior backend engineers — distributed systems, data modelling, latency and throughput are conversations you can hold and challenge; you stay close enough to the code to review a pull request, without needing to be the one writing it

  • Have hands-on experience modernising a large legacy system, ideally extracting services from a monolith, and know how to keep a team delivering while the ground moves

  • Are an effective communicator who can translate company goals into team objectives, and who says the uncomfortable thing early rather than late

  • Think critically and objectively, with a solution-oriented approach that brings people with you

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have worked in a regulated industry such as healthcare or fintech, where privacy and data protection shape design decisions

  • Have navigated hyper-growth environments and understand the trade-offs they force on architecture and team organisation

  • Have formed a considered view on AI coding assistants — their real benefits and their real shortcomings

Life at Doctolib Tech

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack in this product area is Ruby on Rails and TypeScript/React in the monolith, Kotlin for new services, with Postgres, Redis and Kafka underneath.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here.

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site.

  • A Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass) fully paid for by Doctolib

  • Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

  • Subsidized sports membership through our partner Urban Sports Club

  • Relocation support in case of international mobility

title: Intern Talent Acquisition Coordinator (x/f/m)
description:
Doctolib is looking for a Talent Acquisition Coordinator to join the Tech & Product Talent Acquisition team in our Berlin office. 

As a Coordinator, you'll focus on three essential areas: delivering exceptional candidate experience, mastering complex tech & product interview scheduling, and continuously improving our interview processes. In this role, you'll gain comprehensive insight into recruitment while applying your organisational and project management skills in a fast-paced, high-volume environment and developing advanced people skills through multi-stakeholder management. 

What you’ll do

As an intern, you will support us in the following areas:

  • Coordinate interviews between candidates, Hiring Managers and tech interviewers, ensuring a smooth candidate experience.

  • Send critical candidate communication during the recruitment process. 

  • Help maintain accurate candidate and interview information in our Applicant Tracking System.

  • Manage complex interviewer pools, candidate information and interview supporting materials.

  • Adapt and streamline the scheduling process to suit candidates and business needs.

  • Contribute to interview process design, track scheduling metrics (time to schedule, time to interview) and own your own projects with a focus on process improvement while leveraging AI and automation tools. 

  • Collaborate with Talent Acquisition Partners and Hiring Managers on Tech & Product recruitment end to end processes.

Working with us, you will learn:

  • How the full Talent Acquisition process works, from application to onboarding.

  • How to coordinate recruitment processes in an international technology environment.

  • How to work with an Applicant Tracking System and recruitment-related data.

  • How to collaborate with candidates, Hiring Managers and internal stakeholders.

  • How to contribute to a positive and inclusive candidate experience.

  • How Talent Acquisition supports the growth of Tech & Product teams.

Who you are 

If you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You could be our next teammate if you:

  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, sense of urgency, and agility that enable you to stay on top of priorities and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Strong empathy that allows you to put yourself in other people's shoes and a genuine passion for finding solutions that work best for everyone.

  • A curious, problem-solving mindset with a willingness to learn and dig deeper to understand how operations and processes work.

  • Comfortable leveraging AI tools to streamline daily tasks, draft communications, and improve efficiency, with curiosity to keep learning new AI-powered ways of working.

  • Fluency in English with strong verbal and written communication skills, allowing you to adapt your expression to different audiences and situations.

Now, it would be fantastic if you:

  • Speak German at B2 level or above.

  • Have previous experience with an Applicant Tracking System, HR administration or coordination.

  • Have experience in an international, technology or fast-paced environment.

What we offer 

  • A structured and personalised onboarding programme through our Doctolib Academy, as well as a wide range of in-house training opportunities.

  • A flexible working model that allows for hybrid and office-based work.

  • A Deutschlandticket sponsored by Doctolib, or reimbursement of your semester ticket, subject to the applicable eligibility rules.

  • 28 vacation days per year, calculated pro rata according to your working schedule and internship duration.

  • Regular breakfast in the office and subsidies for your lunch or grocery shopping.

  • A subsidised sports programme with our partner Urban Sports Club.

The Interview Process

  • First call with Hiring Manager (30’)

  • Case study Interview (60’)

Job Details

  • Internship in full-time (40h/week).

  • Duration: 6 months.

  • Workplace: Berlin

  • Salary: €1,900 gross/month for a mandatory internship.

  • Salary: €2,425 gross/month for a voluntary internship; €2,545 gross/month from 1 January 2027

  • Start date: As soon as possible

  • Opportunity to work in a hybrid setup (3 office days/week).

description:

We're looking for a Localization Operations Manager to audit and redesign how we conduct translation and localization end to end; from content creation, through engineering delivery, to linguistic quality review.   • Audit the current end-to-end localization and translation workflow for our three main markets, from source content definition through engineering execution to linguistic QA, defining and implementing improvements for an updated localization process. 

  • Evaluate and evolve our use of machine translation and AI-assisted translation tooling, including glossary ownership and governance, content classification, and where and how human review fits in.

  • Define a vendor and tooling strategy for translation and linguistic quality a cross our language markets; updating our existing tool stack as needed. 

  • Design and roll-out evolved processes in partnership with engineering, design, product, medical, and local go-to-market teams

  • Hand off a durable process and toolset by the end of the engagement.

Who you are

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Prior experience as a Technical Program Manager, Product Manager, or Localization Operations Manager, with hands-on experience designing and implementing localization/internationalization tooling and MT/AI-assisted translation workflows.

  • Strong proficiency in AI-native workflows as they relate to software development and content management. Can build tooling solutions, agents, and technical solutions where needed. 

  • Experience with multi-market, multi-language products at scale. Italian, French or German localization experience is a plus.

  • Track record of shipping quality, speed, or cost improvements to a localization or translation operation.

  • Strong stakeholder management across design, engineering, and content teams.

  • Comfortable working independently on a fixed-term, outcome-driven engagement.

In this role, you will contribute to making medical information clear, structured, and usable across products for patients, healthcare professionals, and technical teams.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Collect and format sets of terms describing pathologies, allergies, treatments, and other medical concepts, based on standard medical terminologies such as ICD-10 and SNOMED CT.

  • Adapt medical labels to create versions that are understandable to patients and healthcare professionals.

  • Translate labels from English into German.

  • Map medical lists of terms across different products.

  • Select and filter terms, then validate your choices with medical experts.

  • Share your work and methodology with the Terminology and Ontology team and product teams.

  • Deliver sets of terms to technical teams in the correct format.



About our data environment

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to the country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack is composed of Dagster, dbt, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, and other technologies.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here and learn about our first AI hackathon here!

If you would like to find out more about tech life at Doctolib, feel free to read our latest Medium blog articles!

Who you are

Before you read on, if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You could be our next teammate if:

  • You have medical skills gained through a diploma or degree that includes medical-domain learning.

  • You have knowledge of data management.

  • You are familiar with medical terminologies such as ICD-10 and SNOMED CT.

  • You have strong spreadsheet skills, including Google Sheets or Excel and the use of formulas. 

  • You are attentive to detail and demonstrate rigour in your work.

  • You speak German and English, which is a must have for this role.

Nice to have:

  • Experience using AI tools such as Claude.

  • Python programming skills.

  • Additional depth of medical knowledge.

  • Dutch language skills.

 

What we offer

  • A structured and personalized onboarding program through our Doctolib Academy, as well as a wide range of in-house training opportunities and masterclasses throughout the internship.

  • Regular breakfast in the office and subsidies for your lunch or grocery shopping.

  • A Deutschlandticket sponsored by Doctolib, or reimbursement of your semester ticket.

  • A flexible workplace policy offering up to 2 days of hybrid work per week.

 

The interview process

  • An interview with our Talent Partner (30 minutes).

  • An interview with the hiring manager (30 minutes).

Job details

  • Contract Type: Internship (Mandatory/Voluntary)

  • Working Time: Full-time

  • Duration: 6 months

  • Work model: Hybrid

  • Location: Berlin, Germany.

  • Expected start date: January 2027

title: Senior Software Engineer - Node.js/TypeScript (x/f/m)
description:
Set a new pulse for healthcare!

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the DIAL team in the Phone Assistant domain.

Your mission will be to design, build, and scale the AI-powered features that transform how practitioners and patients connect over the phone — making care more accessible for patients and reducing administrative burden for health professionals. You will work in a feature team developing the Phone Assistant, Doctolib's solution that combines LLM reasoning, speech recognition, and real-time backend systems, launching first in Germany and expanding to France and Italy. 

Working in the tech team at Doctolib means building innovative products and features to improve the daily lives of care teams and patients.

What you'll do

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Build and operate backend services in Node.js/TypeScript (with Python exposure), designing for reliability, scalability, and real-time performance

  • Design, evaluate, and ship LLM-based features end-to-end: prompt engineering, tool calling, structured outputs, guardrails, and fallback strategies

  • Own AI feature quality: build evaluation datasets and scorers (e.g., in Braintrust), track regressions, and make evidence-based ship decisions before each release

  • Deploy and operate cloud-native services on Kubernetes across major cloud providers (AWS/Azure/GCP), and evolve CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions

  • Design data models and drive database migrations and performance tuning for real-time workloads (PostgreSQL: connection pooling, indexing, query optimisation)

  • Maintain a high testing bar (unit, integration, e2e), debug distributed systems in production with strong observability, and contribute to pragmatic, secure architecture decisions

Who you are

Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Have 5+ years of backend engineering experience building scalable, resilient systems in Node.js/TypeScript (with some Python)

  • Have hands-on production experience building LLM-based features: prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, eval frameworks, and handling real-world failure modes

  • Have proven experience deploying and operating services on Kubernetes within at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP), with solid CI/CD practices

  • Have a strong testing culture (unit/integration/e2e), sharp debugging skills for microservices and distributed systems, and a focus on code quality

  • Are fluent in English, with a collaborative mindset and the drive to own problems end-to-end — from design to production

It would be fantastic if you:

  • Have experience with speech pipelines (ASR, TTS, streaming audio) or voice agents

  • Are familiar with event-driven architectures and message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, or Redis Streams), and have hands-on PostgreSQL experience (EXPLAIN/ANALYZE, indexing strategies, connection pooling)

  • Have an interest in telephony and real-time communication (SIP, RTP, WebRTC) — no prior experience needed, we will teach you

Life at Doctolib Tech

  • Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile app interfaces, multiple languages, and is adapted to country and healthcare specialty requirements.

  • Our stack is composed of Rails, TypeScript, Java, Python, Kotlin, Swift, and React Native.

  • We leverage AI ethically across our products to empower patients and health professionals. Discover our AI vision here.

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site.

What we offer

  • A Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass) fully paid for by Doctolib

  • 28 vacation days + 1 additional day for each full calendar year of employment (up to a maximum of 30 days)

  • Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

  • Company health insurance with great supplementary benefits through our partner Allianz

  • Company pension scheme (bAV) through Allianz with an employer subsidy of 40% (15% within the probationary period)

  • The Doctolib Parent Care program, which includes one month additional parental leave and much more

  • Enrollment in Doctolib's long-term employee value sharing plan called DoctoGrowth

  • Free mental health and coaching services through our partner Moka.care

  • Subsidized sports membership through our partner Urban Sports Club

  • A flexible workplace policy offering both hybrid and office-based mode

  • Alongside healthy snacks and our regular breakfast buffet, we provide a subsidized meal benefit

  • For caregivers and workers with disabilities, a package including an adaptation of the remote policy, extra days off for medical reasons, and psychological support

  • Relocation support in case of international mobility

  • Access to the best AI tools for coding, development and dedicated training

Our interview process

  • Recruiter Interview

  • Live Coding Interview

  • System Design Interview

  • Behavioral Interview

  • At least one reference check

We want your experience to be clear, respectful, and transparent. Learn more about our hiring process on our candidate experience page.

Job details

  • Permanent position

  • Tech stack: Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Kubernetes, AWS/Azure/GCP, PostgreSQL

  • Full-time

  • Berlin

  • Hybrid work setup (up to 2 remote days per week)

  • Start date: as soon as possible

We welcome everyone

At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. This translates into our recruitment process. We evaluate candidates based solely on qualifications and motivation, without any form of discrimination.

The more diverse ideas are heard, the more our product will truly improve healthcare for all. You are welcome to apply to Doctolib, regardless of your gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or disability.

To ensure equal opportunities, we invite you to exclude personal information (e.g., pictures, age) from your applications. If you require any accommodation, please let us know for support during the hiring process.

Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of!

description:

Der deutsche Gesundheitsmarkt befindet sich an einem entscheidenden Wendepunkt. Als Account Executive (x/f/m) im Vertriebsgebiet Dreieck Solingen, Bergisch Gladbach und Gummersbach (rechtsrheinisch) führst Du Dein Territory wie ein eigenes Business und bringst mit unserer KI-gestützten All-in-One-Lösung echten Mehrwert direkt in den Praxisalltag.

Du gewinnst neue Zahnarztpraxen für Doctolib und begleitest sie auf dem Weg zu einer effizienteren, digitaleren Organisation. Die Chance, die vor uns liegt, ist noch weit größer als das, was wir bisher aufgebaut haben.

 

Deine Aufgaben

  • Outbound und Inbound Sales: Du kombinierst die aktive Ansprache potenzieller Kund:innen über bereitgestellte Leads, telefonisch und vor Ort, mit der Bearbeitung eingehender Inbound-Anfragen. Dein Ziel ist es, qualifizierte Ersttermine zu vereinbaren und neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten zu entwickeln.

  • Erste Verkaufsgespräche und Bedarfsermittlung: Du führst erste Gespräche mit Zahnärzt:innen und Praxisteams, verstehst ihre Herausforderungen und identifizierst ihren individuellen Bedarf.

  • Full-Cycle-Sales: Du verantwortest den gesamten Sales Cycle, von der ersten Kontaktaufnahme über die Bedarfsermittlung, Produktpräsentation und Verhandlung bis zum erfolgreichen Abschluss.

  • Pipeline, Umsatz und Wachstum: Du baust Deine Pipeline eigenständig auf und verantwortest die Entwicklung Deines Vertriebsgebiets.

  • Kundenzentrierte Beratung: Du zeigst potenziellen Kund:innen den konkreten Mehrwert unserer digitalen HealthTech-Lösung für ihren Praxisalltag.

  • Datengetriebene Erfolgsmessung: Du trackst Deine Performance regelmäßig mit Salesforce und nutzt Daten für eine gezielte Vertriebsstrategie.

  • Strukturierte Übergabe nach Vertragsabschluss: Nach dem Abschluss übergibst Du Deine neuen Kund:innen strukturiert an unser Projektmanagement-Team. Dort werden sie anschließend vollständig betreut und bis zur erfolgreichen Umsetzung begleitet.

Die Position ist vollständig auf die Gewinnung neuer Kund:innen ausgerichtet. Eine laufende Bestandskundenbetreuung gehört nicht zu Deinen Aufgaben.

Dein Profil

Du bist der festen Überzeugung, dass Du genau das mitbringst, was es für die Position braucht? Dann ermutigen wir Dich, Dich zu bewerben. Selbst wenn Du nicht jede Anforderung erfüllst, bist Du vielleicht genau die oder der richtige zukünftige Doctoliber:in für diese oder andere Stellen.

  • Sales ist Deine Welt: Du hast mindestens zwei bis drei Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb, idealerweise im Außendienst und im Neukundengeschäft

  • Proaktivität und Akquise-Talent: Du hast bereits eigenständig Pipeline aufgebaut und neue Kund:innen gewonnen

  • Beratungsstärke: Du kannst erklärungsbedürftige Produkte oder Dienstleistungen verständlich und kundenzentriert vermitteln

  • Energie und Überzeugungskraft: Du trittst sicher und professionell auf, verkaufst mit Leidenschaft und lässt Dich auch von Rückschlägen nicht entmutigen

title: Senior AI Specialist (Operations) (x/f/m)
description:
Doctolib is looking for you to join us as a Senior AI Specialist (x/f/m) at our Berlin location, starting as soon as possible.

Doctolib is becoming an AI-native company. We are redesigning the way we work, workflow by workflow, and are looking for people who will not only support this transformation, but actively build it. As a Senior AI Specialist, you will be the technical builder and AI Ops Owner behind AI-powered productivity for our Operations and Customer Success teams.

 

You will work in founder and product mode: you will own a workflow end to end, from context and agent design to evaluation, and continuously take it to a higher level of automation. Our ambition is to move away from manual case-by-case work towards workflows that run largely autonomously while maintaining a high quality bar. In this way, you will contribute directly to our mission of improving healthcare for everyone.

Your Responsibilities

  • Redesign workflows rather than simply automating them: You analyze the most critical Operations and Customer Success workflows, break down time-consuming processes that require limited judgment, and transform them through the use of AI agents. You set clear objectives for autonomy and quality, and continuously develop them further.

  • Build and operate AI agents as products: You develop and manage agents on platforms such as Dust or Claude. Each agent is deployed to production with a defined baseline and relevant metrics such as benefit, usage, and scalability.

  • Knowledge and context management: You deliberately curate the context agents need, from templates to core data. The guiding principle is quality over quantity. You ensure that knowledge sources in Confluence, Drive, or Salesforce are always up to date and well structured.

  • Evaluation and quality assurance: You define quality standards and establish evaluation routines to identify and address weaknesses such as hallucinations or prompt drift at an early stage. You continuously optimize prompts through systematic user feedback and A/B testing.

  • CRM and data integration: You own the interfaces between CRM systems such as Salesforce and our AI platforms. You automate data flows and work closely with IT to unlock new, valuable data sources for our agents.

  • Central interface and enablement: You translate business requirements into technical solutions and bring together stakeholders from Leadership, IT, and Product. You strengthen the team’s AI fluency in the areas of context, agent management, and evaluation.

  • Impact and measurement: Rather than inventing new KPIs, you make the success of AI measurable using existing metrics such as time, quality, and cost, and use these insights to guide the next steps in scaling.

Your Profile

Since production-ready AI workflows and agent technologies are still relatively new, years of market experience are rare. We therefore deliberately prioritize potential over years of experience alone. What matters to us is your ability to learn quickly, your strong product mindset, and your judgment. If you are passionate about this field and bring the necessary skills, we would be delighted to hear from you, even if your profile does not perfectly cover every single aspect.

What Really Matters to Us, Regardless of the Specific Tool:

  • Learning speed and a production mindset: You have taught yourself a new technical field from scratch and built something real that people actually used. You can describe precisely what went wrong, such as hallucinations, prompt drift, outdated data, or costs, and how you solved it.

  • An instinct for evaluation: You do not rely on something merely “looking good”. You define a quality bar and measure against it. For you, automation and quality go hand in hand.

  • Ownership and communication: You take ownership of a problem end to end, prioritize rigorously, feel comfortable with ambiguity, and make technical topics understandable to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Technical and data understanding: You can read and adapt scripts, understand APIs, webhooks, and automation tools such as Make, n8n, and Zapier, and know how CRM data, ideally Salesforce data, flows into AI systems.

  • Strong communication skills: You have a confident command of English and can operate at the highest level in our international environment. German at B1 level is sufficient.

We Are Particularly Interested in:

  • Expertise with agent platforms: You have practical experience with systems such as Dust, Claude, or LangChain. Since tools evolve quickly, we primarily rely on your process understanding and evaluation skills as a sustainable foundation.

  • Technical depth and data fluency: You are proficient in languages such as Python or JavaScript and can confidently navigate Salesforce architectures or BI environments such as Tableau and Metabase to manage data flows effectively.

  • Operations experience: You have solid experience working with scaled Customer Success or Operations teams and understand their specific dynamics.

What We Offer

  • A Germany-wide public transport pass sponsored by Doctolib if you work from the office or in hybrid mode

  • Company-sponsored health insurance with excellent additional benefits

  • 28 days of paid vacation, plus one additional day for every full calendar year of employment, up to a maximum of 30 days

  • Participation in Doctolib’s long-term employee equity program, DoctoGrowth

  • The opportunity to work from abroad for up to 10 days per year

  • An occupational pension scheme with an employer contribution of 40%, or 15% during the probationary period

  • The Doctolib Parent Care Program, which includes one additional month of parental leave and much more

  • Free mental health and coaching sessions through an external partner

  • In addition to healthy snacks and a regular breakfast buffet, we offer meal vouchers

  • A subsidized sports program with our partner Urban Sports Club

  • For caregivers and employees with disabilities, we offer support that includes more flexible working hours, additional leave for medical reasons, and psychological support

The Interview Process

  • Interview with Talent

  • Hiring Manager interview

  • On-site case study

  • Final interview with VP

  • Reference checks

  • Offer

Job Details

  • Permanent position

  • Full-time

  • Location: Berlin

  • Start date: July

  • Hybrid, 2 days working from home per week

The more diverse our team and ideas are, the more our product can contribute to improving the health of our users. That is why we invite you to apply, regardless of gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, or disability.

 

To ensure equal opportunities, you may omit information such as photos, age, and similar details from your application. Please let us know what accommodations we can make to support you in the best possible way.

We look forward to digitalizing healthcare together with you!

The role

As a Strategy Analyst, you’ll run the projects that decide when and how iwoca contacts its customers through our in-house CRM system. You’ll steer which experiments the team runs, with customer lifetime value as your key metric. You’ll work closely with the Senior CRM Executive, who will bring your changes to life in the messages customers receive. The role will include:

  • Contact strategy. You’ll find the points in the customer journey where a message adds the most value. You’ll weigh the conversion a message brings against the risk of contacting customers too often. You’ll balance short-term gains against long-term customer value, and decide when an automated message is enough and when a person from Operations should step in.

  • Model-driven emails. We’ve started using a model to choose who receives some of our emails. You’ll be responsible for understanding where this approach works well, and collaborate with the data science team to make any improvements.

  • Split tests. You’ll design, run, and interpret controlled experiments on customer contact. For example, you might test the timing and content of emails at key points in the customer journey. You’ll apply statistical thinking so decisions rest on evidence.

  • AI leverage. You know how to use AI to optimise your workflows, for example by checking your analysis or improving your write-ups. You judge when to use it and when not to.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. Wer die Veränderung gestalten will, muss schneller lernen, als sie passiert.

Das heißt auch: Umsetzen ist kein Hexenwerk mehr. Früher war der Job 70, 80 % Entwickeln, das dreht sich gerade. Umsetzung kann man delegieren, Entscheidungen nicht. Darum bist du bei uns der Übersetzer zwischen Fachlichkeit und Technik, und die Ownership für eine Entscheidung trägst du, keine KI.

Das machst du nicht in einem Bodyshop, der dir einen Stuhl beim Kunden besorgt. Und auch nicht in einer Beratung, die nach drei Monaten ein 200-Seiten-Dokument hinterlässt. Wir sitzen über Jahre als tragendes Element in den Entwicklungsteams unserer Kunden, meist in Digitalisierungsteams im Konzern, und schieben dort das ganze Team nach vorne.

Wie du startest

Du kommst in ein bestehendes Projekt mit einem von uns, gehst mit in die Termine und kommst schnell ins Doing, statt ewig Sachen zu lesen. Am Anfang hast du einen Paten, der dich im Team mitnimmt, und einen fachlichen Ansprechpartner. Nach etwa sechs Monaten führst du Termine alleine, setzt Themen eigenständig um und gehst in die Architekturplanung. Stück für Stück übergeben wir dir den Staffelstab, bis du in deinem Bereich die Verantwortung für den Kunden trägst. Leadership heißt bei uns: technische Führung nach außen, nicht nach innen.

Aufgaben

  • Du arbeitest bei einem Kunden, nicht bei dreien gleichzeitig. Mindestens einer von uns ist mit im Projekt, und ihr seid fester Teil der Routinen vom Kundenteam.

  • Du wartest nicht, bis dir jemand eine Aufgabe gibt. Du findest die Aufgaben, stimmst sie ab und übernimmst die Ownership dafür.

  • Ein Ticket ist schön. Und dann reden wir nochmal drüber, wie die Fachlichkeit wirklich ist.

  • Wir sagen nicht Ja und Amen zu allem. Wenn was keinen Sinn macht, sagst du das. Diplomatisch, aber klar.

  • Es geht um den Wert, der beim Kunden entsteht. Dafür baust du sauber und sagst dem Kunden transparent, was der nächste Schritt bringt und was er kostet.

Dein Profil

Was du mitbringst

  • Du bist eher in Fachlichkeiten und im Backend zu Hause als beim nächsten abgespacten UX-Feature. Denn sind wir ehrlich, das bekommt man mittlerweile gut automatisiert.

  • Du hast Architektur nicht nur gesehen, sondern auch verantwortet und gestaltet.

Nice to have

  • Du kennst die Baustoffbranche schon von innen. Einer unserer Kunden ist ein Baustoffhersteller.

Wenn du nicht zu uns passt

  • Du willst ein Team führen. Wir sind zu sechst und planen keine mittlere Führungsebene.

  • Du nutzt KI, um Verantwortung abzugeben, statt deine Entscheidungskraft zu erweitern.

Der Prozess

Kurz und ohne fünf Gesprächsrunden.

  1. Erstgespräch mit mir, 30 Minuten remote. Du prüfst uns dabei genauso wie ich dich. Am Ende sage ich dir direkt, wie ich es sehe, und nicht hinterher in einer kalten Mail.

  2. Kennenlerntag mit dem Team, remote, 4 Stunden mit Pausen. Das ist keine Prüfung. Du reviewst Code und erklärst, was dir auffällt. Du baust mit deinem eigenen KI-Setup einen Fix, so wie du wirklich arbeitest. Und du führst ein Kundengespräch im Rollenspiel und lernst das Team in 1:1s kennen. Unsere Werte

title: Integration Specialist – Electronic Data Interchange (EDI)
description:
We Want You to Grow With Us 

We are strengthening our EDI integration capabilities at Intersnack IT. As our next Integration Specialist – EDI, you will bring your experience in electronic data interchange and your understanding of business processes to support reliable transactions between our business units, trading partners and applications.

Your knowledge of Order to Cash (O2C) and Source to Pay (S2P) will help you translate business requirements into effective integration solutions. Based in Düsseldorf, you will work closely with our Application Service Delivery & Support and Business Transformation teams, business stakeholders and external EDI providers, supporting both daily operations and international ERP initiatives.

What We Can Offer 

This position combines hands-on EDI development with responsibility for integrations that support our supply chain. You will apply your business process knowledge to practical technical solutions and contribute to global ERP initiatives and local EDI rollouts.

If you bring strong EDI expertise and experience with O2C and S2P processes, we can support your onboarding into the Infor M3 integration stack. You will build on your existing knowledge while becoming familiar with our applications, mapping tools and integration environment.

You will join a supportive, international IT team, working alongside colleagues and specialist providers with opportunities to deepen your expertise in integration delivery and EDI operations.

How You Will Spend Your Time as Our Next Integration Specialist – EDI 

You will connect business requirements with the technical delivery and operation of EDI integrations. Your work will span document mapping, integration configuration, rollout support and daily troubleshooting, helping ensure that transactions are processed reliably across our Infor applications and external EDI networks.

What You Will Do 

  • Translate business requirements and trading partner specifications into practical EDI solutions, supporting document flows across Order to Cash, Logistics and Source to Pay.

  • Create and maintain complex document mappings, transforming partner messages into standard XML formats and vice versa.

  • Develop, configure and maintain EDI integrations across Infor M3, Infor ION, Infor OS and Infor Enterprise Collaborator (IEC/MEC).

  • Define and maintain mapping standards, data validation rules and interface specifications, supported by clear functional and technical documentation.

  • Support EDI workstreams within global ERP initiatives and local rollouts across business units, maintaining consistency with global integration templates.

  • Monitor daily EDI transactions, prioritise critical issues and resolve integration or transmission failures to help prevent supply chain disruptions.

  • Analyse performance across EDI networks and clearing centres, identify recurring errors and bottlenecks, and coordinate configuration adjustments and testing with external providers.

  • Maintain standard messages and application interfaces in line with relevant industry standards and data compliance requirements.

  • Collaborate with internal IT teams, business stakeholders and external providers to deliver and support integrations involving both Infor and other applications.

What We Expect of You 

Essential Skills & Experience 

  • Strong familiarity with the document sequences supporting core supply chain processes such as Order to Cash (O2C) , Logistics and Source to Pay (S2P), including orders, invoices and shipping notices.

  • Extensive hands-on experience in Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), B2B integration frameworks and complex data mapping environments.

  • Strong technical proficiency in EDI mapping tools, XML schemas and data transformation languages.

  • Good awareness of global B2B messaging standards, such as EDIFACT, and electronic communication protocols.

Almost every company running SAP faces the same task: the move to SAP S/4HANA. These programmes run for years, cost tens of millions, and regularly stall at the same point. Nobody fully understands the legacy landscape that has grown over decades.

That is where Qorelo comes in. We are building the AI platform for S/4HANA transformation. Qorelo reads code, processes, documentation and how the system is actually used, makes the existing landscape transparent, and delivers the fit-to-standard analysis in weeks instead of months. The knowledge stays with the customer afterwards, long after the system integrators have moved on.

We have raised $3.5M from HPI Ventures, the fund tied to the institute of SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, along with other strong backers. We already work with Fortune 500 and DAX 40 companies and we work with SAP consultancies who use Qorelo in their own client projects.


The role

As Head of Operations, you make sure what we sell actually goes live, and that the company behind it runs without friction. Your job is to make our customers successful and to free up the founders, sales and engineering to do the work only they can do.

We are growing from a small founding team into a company that runs several enterprise rollouts at once, works with SAP consultancy partners, and is hiring across engineering, sales and product. That growth needs one person who owns how it all fits together.

You report directly to the founders and our diffrent department Heads. This is not an admin role. Half of it sits right next to the customer.

What you'll own

  • Customer delivery and onboarding. From signature to live. You run the rollout plan with our Forward Deployed Engineers and solution architects: kick-off, access and security onboarding, milestones, steering meetings. You make sure every customer reaches value on time, and you spot the risk before it becomes an escalation.

  • Commercial operations. Contracts, order forms, framework agreements, procurement and supplier onboarding at enterprise customers, invoicing and collections. You make the paper process predictable so deals close faster and cash comes in on time.

  • Partner operations. We work with SAP consultancies and system integrators who use Qorelo in their own client projects. You set up and run how that works in practice: agreements, enablement, joint delivery, reporting.

  • Finance and planning. Budget, burn and runway tracking, monthly reporting, board and investor material, together with our external tax advisor and accountants. You know the numbers and can explain them.

  • People operations. Hiring process, onboarding, contracts, payroll setup, equity administration, tools. Every new joiner is productive in their first week.

What you need

  • 4+ years in operations, delivery or customer-facing project roles, with at least 2 years at a B2B software startup or scale-up.

  • You have worked in or around the SAP ecosystem, at a consultancy, system integrator or SAP software vendor, and know how a transformation programme runs.

  • You have been an early operations, chief of staff or COO hire at a startup and built the operating backbone from scratch.

  • You have worked with partners or resellers and know what it takes to make a channel deliver.

title: AI Engineering Manager
description:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Our ambition is to put AI capability in every worker’s hands. Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. Now Mastry, our new adaptive learning platform, takes that further, guiding a company’s AI workforce transformation from start to finish. Mae, our AI guide inside Mastry, is a real-time AI agent that thinks, speaks, listens and sees, working alongside the tools you already use, like Claude and Copilot.

We closed our latest fundraising round in April 2026, with $500m+ raised in total from VC partners including Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Schroders Capital and Lightspeed. With a $2.1bn valuation, we are Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn, and we are just getting started.

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.

Why this role exists

Every foundation model lab is solving the same problem: build more capability. Almost nobody is solving the harder one — what happens when that capability meets a real organisation and real people who have to relearn how they work. That's the adoption layer, still wide open, and Multiverse sits in the unique position to solve this problem with ten years of proprietary learner and employer data driven from 1,500+ companies that no one else has.

Diagnose & Prescribe (D&P) is the engine room of that problem. It works out what a learner or employer actually needs, then decides what they get funded for and which apprenticeship or learning path they're pointed to next. D&P is how we assess a learner's or employer's skill gaps, decide what they need, and point them to the right apprenticeship or learning path — so the blast radius here is human and financial, not just a dashboard metric.

The line between leading this team and building the product has already blurred, which is why this role exists as it does. We need a leader who stays close enough to the work to have credible judgment in it, and who builds a high-trust team where diverse perspectives actually make the problem-solving better.

This is a broad, domain-coherent, event-driven and increasingly AI-native estate. The dominant challenge isn't deep algorithmic difficulty in any single repo — it's holding the whole D&P picture, sequencing work across varied services, and keeping load-bearing decisions safe as the system evolves underneath you.

What you're signing up for

  • A genuinely unsolved problem — the constraint here is people and adoption, not model capability.

  • High agency. We set outcomes, not playbooks. You and your team define how this evolves.

  • Real commercial breadth. This team sits at the intersection of Product, go-to-market, and eligibility — closer to the customer than most engineering roles.

  • Craft that's respected, not traded off. Strict typing, layered testing, ADRs, observability — and AI-native ways of working as the baseline, not an experiment.

  • A company mid-transformation, told straight. Multiverse is rebuilding itself into a product-powered, AI-native company in real time. You're not inheriting a finished system — you're one of the people defining it.

What you'll do

You will own delivery, technical direction, and team health in the D&P service estate — the full learner and customer journey from diagnosis through prescription to onboarding and growth tracking. Concretely, that means leading the team(s) across surfaces like:

  • Diagnosis & needs assessment — AI-heavy services (retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), LLM-scored assessment) that turn raw signal into a picture of where a learner or employer actually is.

  • Prescription & eligibility — build the product which helps learners and customers understand the best learning course for their skills and career development, that leverages a customer's levy funds. Much of this is load-bearing logic with a genuine financial and regulatory blast radius.

  • Recommendation & onboarding — turning a diagnosis into the right prescribed path and getting learners into it, where those decisions become visible to customers and learners.

  • The platform arc — continuing to carve D&P logic out of the shared legacy monolith into dedicated services, while backing the newer AI-native product from beta toward scale.

  • Coach and build the team. Hire well, give every report a real growth plan, and move the team into a high-performing, AI-native operating rhythm — promotions and performance issues are never a surprise.

  • Stay hands-on. Whiteboard distributed designs, review and negotiate the RabbitMQ event schemas and API contracts that ripple across services, and write production code yourself when it's the fastest way to de-risk or unblock.

  • Deliver predictably. Use cycle time, change failure rate, and MTTR to balance shipping speed, debt, and change-safety on logic with genuine financial and regulatory blast radius.

  • Raise the AI-native bar. Prove better discovery-to-build-to-review loops on your own team and share what works across engineering.

  • Partner on strategy. Work directly with Product and Design — and closely with go-to-market — to turn learner and customer behaviour into technical direction on the surfaces where eligibility and recommendation decisions become visible to real customers.

What we need

A few terms you'll see below: D&P (Diagnose & Prescribe, this team's name), BAM (our hiring framework — Behaviour, Achievement, Mastery), ADRs (architecture decision records), IfATE (the UK body governing apprenticeship standards).

  • Engineering management of full-stack teams shipping production software, with real technical depth to review architecture and challenge design.

  • A team you led has shipped AI features to real users and operated them — not a side experiment.

  • Strong Python/TypeScript (if you don’t have Typescript, you will need to learn): React/Next.js (App Router, RSC, server actions), tRPC/GraphQL, Node/Express.

  • PostgreSQL at scale via an ORM, with migration discipline on large, live schemas.

  • Event-driven systems on a message bus (we use RabbitMQ) — versioned events, idempotency, backward-compatible migration.

  • A high engineering maturity bar as second nature: typing, testing, feature flags, ADRs, CI/CD, observability.

  • AI-native delivery in practice — you build daily with Claude Code, Cursor, or the current best tool, and understand context management, model selection, tool design, and the token economics that separate a prototype from an affordable production system.

What sets you apart

  • GTM/acquisition-funnel experience — you've owned surfaces where onboarding and eligibility meet real customers.

  • Strangler-pattern pragmatism — legacy monolith and greenfield edge-native product, at the same time.

  • Accessibility and UX as defaults on learner-facing surfaces, not afterthoughts.

Not for you if

This role won't fit if you'd rather run ceremonies than stay in the system, the design, and the code yourself. It also won't fit if you see AI tooling as a productivity tweak rather than a step change in how a team works. And it needs someone who renegotiates the scope out loud when it's wrong, not someone who absorbs it and hopes it works out.

Stack & how we lead

TypeScript core (React/Next.js, Node) with PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ as the event backbone, plus Python and Elixir services — from RAG pipelines to a Claude-powered edge-native product. GitHub, CircleCI, Datadog. AI-assisted development is first-class, not bolted on.

You'll lead full-stack engineers (with Python/Elixir specialists), report to the Senior Director of Engineering for Diagnose & Prescribe, and calibrate regularly with a peer group of EMs — you're not doing this alone. We reject micro-management: we set the objective, you and your team own the how. Kindness, candour, and curiosity over hierarchy — bad news travels as fast as good.

Benefits

  • Health and wellbeing: Bupa private medical insurance, a medical cash back plan, therapy through Spill and gym access through Wellhub.

  • Family support: enhanced maternity and paternity leave, adoption and shared parental leave, paid leave after pregnancy loss, and a workplace nursery scheme.

  • Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office - except for Coaches & Instructors who come into the office 1 day per month. Plus 10 days a year to work from anywhere.

  • Work perks: quarterly team socials, company-wide events, happy hours, lunch delivered to the office once a week, fully stocked snack bar and a drinks fridge!

The world's largest companies compete by being different, and most of that difference lives in the software they've built for themselves, which decides everything from how parcels reach your door to how food gets onto supermarket shelves. That software is a real advantage, but it's also the hardest part of the business to change safely, so good ideas often wait months or even years for the systems to catch up.

Every large enterprise has a software company hiding inside it, and Conduct is building the operating system for it. We read a company's code and processes, work out what needs to change, and help the business and its systems move forward together, wherever custom software has become too complex to change safely.

Fortune Global 500 companies like DHL and Daimler Truck already trust us with their most critical systems, and we've just raised a $60M Series A from Index Ventures, ICONIQ and SAP.

We're a talent-dense team of about 70, growing fast across London and New York, with people from Palantir, G-Research, Legora and Sequoia. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here will shape the company and how the world's largest companies operate.

About the role

Our go-to-market team is growing fast in London and New York, and over the next year we'll scale it several times over, with new account executives and regional directors joining across both offices. They sell a technical product to CIOs and IT leaders at some of the world's largest companies, in long deals with many stakeholders, often alongside partners like SAP and the major consultancies.
